News.title: Burnham pledges more can be done to stop early release for PC Harper’s killers & says ‘I’m looking at everything’
News.content:
PRIME Minister Andy Burnham has said he’ll do everything in his power to stop the early release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers.

After days of confusion and mounting pressure on the government, the PM said he was “increasingly confident” the cop’s smirking killers would remain behind bars.



It follows Angela Rayner’s confirmation on Tuesday that Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole would not be let out under the early release scheme, despite the terms of their exemption not being clearly outlined.

“I am turning over every stone,” he told LBC.



“I am looking at everything. I am pushing the system to go further.

“That’s the way I do my job. I listen to people.”

The PM admitted there was “more that could be done” with regards to this case but that freeing up prison space needn’t be compromised.

“I am confident that we can develop a plan to free up more spaces in the prison estate, so that we can ensure more serious offenders serve their full term,” he said.



Addressing PC Harper’s devastated sister Aimee Harper – who caught the men “sniggering” in court – Mr Burnham said he “felt” for her and was doing everything he could to “lessen [her] anguish”.

He added that IPP prisoners and the return of foreign national offenders warranted similar, considered approaches and that he would not make any “knee-jerk” comments there and then.

It comes after every single police chief in the UK signed a letter on Tuesday urging Andy Burnham to employ “every lawful option” to keep Bowers and Cole behind bars.

In an unprecedented move, 50 top police officers united to condemn the government’s justice reforms in a joint missive published by the National Police Chiefs’ Council.

Signatories include the heads of 48 regional forces, alongside leaders from the National Crime Agency and Jersey Police.



The chiefs expressed their alarm over the impact changes to the release policy could have on confidence in the justice system, policing and public protection.

As it stands, Bowers and Cole would be eligible for release under Labour’s new scheme to free up cells, which will see 5000 inmates let out over the course of ten months, starting from October.

After halting the release of over a 1,000 rapists and child sex offenders last week, Mr Burnham said he had reached “the limits” of his intervention powers.

But on Monday night, a government spokesperson said the PM had asked Justice Secretary Alex Norris to consider “further options” to keep more serious offenders – including Andrew’s killers – locked up.

It remains unclear how this exemption will be enforced, given the government has already ruled out implementing special measures for killers of emergency workers.



Exempting “one or two” offenders convicted of manslaughter would be untenable, Downing Street said.

Detective superintendent Stuart Blaik for Thames Valley police suggested excluding those who were more guilty of manslaughter, including PC Harper’s killers, from the scheme.

There are currently 950 prisoners serving sentences for manslaughter in the UK – with hundreds due to be released under the new scheme, instigated by former PM Keir Starmer.

As confusion mounts around PC Harper’s killers’ release, his mum Debbie Adlam expressed the agony of not knowing whether justice will be served.

She told ITV’s Good Morning Britain: “I just don’t know how to think, how to feel. It’s turned me inside out.



Separately, she said: “It feels like a hash…a rush job.”

“It feels like nobody’s put enough effort into actually look for reasons or ways. We are having to push on every level. They [Bowers and Cole] weren’t given extreme sentences.

“I’m only asking for them to do what they were given.”

PC Harper, 28, was killed in 2019 after he got caught in ropes towing a stolen quad bike and was dragged along the road.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Henry Long, then 18, who was driving the vehicle, received 16 years in 2020 for manslaughter but will not be eligible for release.



Bowers and Cole, then 17, were also found guilty of manslaughter, but received 13 years due to their younger age.

News.title: Every police chief signs letter urging Burnham to use ‘every lawful option’ to stop early release of PC Harper’s killers
News.content:
EVERY single police chief in the UK has signed a letter urging PM Andy Burnham to use “every lawful option” to keep the killers of PC Andrew Harper behind bars.

In an historic move, 50 top police officers representing every force in the UK have united to condemn Labour’s justice reforms.



Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole were jailed for 13 years in 2020 for the manslaughter of 28-year-old officer Harper.

The government previously claimed it would reportedly face legal challenges if it tried to block the release of Bowers and Cole halfway through their jail terms – a move which sparked outrage across the nation.



Now, top cops across the nation are demanding the Prime Minister abandon plans to grant early freedom to Cole, Bowers and thousands of other dangerous convicts.

The intervention came in an extraordinary joint missive published by the National Police Chiefs’ Council.



Signatories include the heads of 48 UK regional forces, alongside leaders from the National Crime Agency and Jersey Police.

Together, they delivered a scathing rebuke of the Government’s proposed custodial reforms.

Police leaders warned the policy directly endangers the public, damages victim confidence, and erodes trust across the entire justice sector.

They are pressing Mr Burnham to exhaust “every lawful option” to keep the duo behind bars.



The letter explicitly framed the early release policy as a betrayal of the legislation forged in the slain officer’s honor.

PC Harper’s widow, Lissie, has campaigned tirelessly for Harper’s Law following national outrage over the sentences handed to her husband’s killers.

The landmark law mandated life sentences for anyone who slays an emergency worker in the line of duty.



Chiefs voiced deep alarm over the erosion of judicial authority, questioning how families can trust the courts when sentences are drastically cut after the fact.

The letter added: “We do not suggest that the grief of a police family is greater than that of any other bereaved family, nor that the life of an emergency worker has greater value.”

Chief constables fear that the early release scheme will endanger the public, warning: “This is not simply a question of punishment. It is a question of ensuring that public protection, victim confidence and community safety remain central to decisions that may substantially reduce the time an offender spends in custody.’

Now they want release decisions to consider “the impact that significant changes to release policy may have on victims, public protection, policing and confidence in the justice system”.

The missive cautioned that freeing the killers sends a damaging message to serving personnel who “will question what message this sends about the value placed on their service and sacrifice when they put themselves in harm’s way to protect others”.



Concluding their plea, the chiefs wrote: “We make this request in memory of PC Andrew Harper, in support of his family, friends, colleagues and the communities he served and on behalf of all victims of serious offending.

“The public should be able to trust that when a court passes sentence for the most serious crimes, victims, public protection and confidence in the justice system remain at the heart of any subsequent decisions about release.”

Newly-married PC Harper died after getting caught up in a strap attached to the rear of a car.



He was dragged more than a mile as the killers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berks, in 2019.

Bowers and Cole, both 17 at the time of the crime, got 13 years in 2020 after being convicted of manslaughter and remain eligible to be freed in January, just halfway through their sentences.

Hopes were raised for PC Harper’s family when the PM ordered a review of the scheme.

Changes were made including preventing rapists and paedophiles from being let out early — but not include those convicted of manslaughter like Bowers and Cole.

However, government spokesperson said on Monday night that the new PM has been pushing to exempt the duo from the early release scheme.



Andy Burnham reportedly asked Justice Secretary Alex Norris to find a way to keep the pair locked up.

The PM has said he does not want any lags let out early and has asked for three areas to be examined with a view to this aim.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He wants to increase the rate at which foreign criminals are sent back to their country of origin.

He is also looking to fix the dispute over Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentences — abolished in 2012 — under which more than 2,300 people are indefinitely detained or trapped in a cycle of lifelong recall, and the release of lower-risk offenders.

News.title: Shocking moment ferry floats upside down on lake after capsizing as 15 killed and 27 missing
News.content:
THIS is the harrowing moment an overloaded ferry lies upside down after capsizing – killing 15 people and leaving 27 missing.

Shocking footage shows the grim aftermath of the disaster on Zimbabwe’s Lake Kariba.



The overturned vessel can be seen floating in the vast lake as rescue teams race to find survivors.

Zimbabwe’s national management agency said 77 people had been rescued and made it to a small island in the lake.



State broadcaster ZBC published footage of speedboats making their way towards the capsized ferry as a helicopter hovered overhead.

An underwater search-and-rescue operation is also underway in a desperate bid to recover those still missing.

Zimbabwe’s Civil Protection Unit said it could only confirm from ticket sales that 114 adults were onboard, along with five crew members.

The true number of people on the ferry is believed to have been much higher.



The agency said there may also have been an unknown number of children below the ticketing age who were onboard but were not accounted for.

The ferry had a capacity of just 90 people, according to the agency, which recommended that the disaster be officially declared.

Mutsa Murombedzi, a local MP, posted a video she said showed people waving goodbye to the ageing ferry as it set off on its journey.

She said some people standing on the shore had expressed concern that the ferry would not withstand the strong waves on the lake.

Murombedzi said the vessel was used by rural communities to travel across the lake.



An investigation is now ongoing to determine the exact circumstances of the tragic incident.

This comes after a ferry carrying 116 passengers capsized off the coast of Guyana.

The MV Barima, bound for the port of Kaituma, issued a distress call at around 11pm local time as the vessel began to sink.

Guyanese Prime Minister Mark Phillips said 67 people, including 15 children, were rescued alive.

Another ferry was sent to the area to provide emergency medical treatment and care to survivors.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The MV Barima is understood to have departed Georgetown at around 3pm on Saturday.

The ageing vessel was built in 1939 and measures 40m (131ft) in length, according to a listing on VesselFinder.

News.title: Windmill ordered to repaint after row over bright colours as local says first miller would be ‘rolling in his grave’
News.content:
SPINNING MAD Windmill ordered to repaint after row over bright colours as local says first miller would be ‘rolling in his grave’

THE owner of a windmill has been told to strip its bright paintwork, with a local complaining that the first miller would be “rolling in his grave” at the sight of it.

Richard Holt, 33, painted Melin Llynon – a 250-year-old Grade-II listed windmill in Anglesey – for the week-long youth festival, Urdd Eisteddfod.



Richard had planned on repainting it once the youth festival was over but decided to keep the colour scheme – which mirrors a Welsh youth group’s mascot – after receiving a flood of positive comments.

Not all the locals approve however, including Dr Eiddwen Jones, 85, the great-great-great-great-granddaughter of Thomas Jones, first miller of Melin Llynon.



Thomas managed the property for 70 years in the village of Llanddeusant until he died in his nineties.

“He would have turned in his grave; he wouldn’t have liked it knowing the rest of the family and knowing what they like and dislike,” she said.



“The colours are vibrant, and I think that the mill should have been in a much nicer whitewash colour.”

“I’m quite happy for it to have been done over that particular period.

“But now is the time to change it back, and of course, as we know, it’s been done without permission of the council.”

The yearly festival attracts around 15,000 people each year, aged eight to 25, and alternates between north and south Wales.

Richard said the windmill’s new colour scheme was intended to bring some joy and celebration to the island.



“Windmills, many, many years ago, back in the day, were always decorated to celebrate really important events,” he said, adding that he had not realised he’d needed permission to repaint it.

However, enthusiastic feedback from locals led him to keep the distinctive paintwork, which has apparently attracted thousands of visitors.

“The demand for it to remain these colours – the Welsh flag colours – was too much to ignore and that’s why it’s still as it is,” he said.

“The feedback we’ve had is that it’s made people feel proud to be Welsh.

“It’s brought colour to the attraction. It’s brought colour to people’s lives. It’s also made the windmill absolutely 100 per cent unique.”



Richard apologised to the council for not requesting permission – but said he did not believe he’d broken the law.

He has since launched a petition calling for the colours to remain.

Hundreds of people have apparently expressed their support for the bold colour scheme, with an opposing petition receiving just three signatures.

An Isle of Anglesey County Council spokesperson explained: “As a council, we fully recognise and support the importance of Welsh culture.

“However, Melin Llynon is a Grade II* listed building, which means it has special architectural and historic significance.



“It is legally protected, and the Council has a statutory duty to ensure there is compliance with The Historic Environment (Wales) Act 2023, which provides for the protection and sustainable management of listed buildings.”

They added that they have asked Richard to remove the paint using the “appropriate conservation method” and that the windmill is returned to a “breathable finish”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The matter remains under investigation, and we are continuing to work with the owner to resolve the situation appropriately,” they said.

News.title: Incredible pics show huge container ship sticking out of water after vessel runs aground and sinks during storm
News.content:
JAW-DROPPING images show a colossal container ship sticking dramatically out of the water after running aground during a vicious storm.

Dramatic footage shows the 1,000ft MSC Silvana VIII heavily submerged off the coast of China, with much of its stern disappearing beneath the waves.



Only the bow and forward section of the vessel remain visible, dramatically raised above the surface.

The Cyprus-flagged ship became stranded near Daishan, in the Zhoushan area of Zhejiang, after being battered by severe weather.



Several attempts to refloat the vessel have reportedly failed.

The ship initially developed only a slight list before seawater began flooding the stern, engine room and several cargo holds.



Around 3,000 tonnes of fuel oil have reportedly been removed from the vessel as part of the salvage operation.

In a shocking development, satellite images reportedly show an oil slick stretching for several miles south of the stricken ship.

Salvage crews now face another major headache as Typhoon Dolphin bears down on the wreckage.

Rough seas and powerful winds are expected to make the already perilous salvage operation even more difficult.



Chinese maritime authorities have established a restricted zone around the vessel and warned members of the public to stay away.

An investigation is under way to establish the exact circumstances surrounding the shocking incident.

This comes as China has evacuated more than one million people as Typhoon Dolphin tears through the country.

Several provinces in the east have been battered by storms and winds of around 100mph, with the extreme weather forcing the cancellation of hundreds of flights.

China’s most powerful typhoon so far this year, it made landfall in Zhejiang, the province south and west of Shanghai, on Sunday evening.



It later weakened to a tropical storm, but its remnants continued to dump heavy rain on eastern provinces including Anhui, Jiangsu and Shandong on Monday.

In Shanghai, China’s second-most populous city, streets were flooded, including in major commercial districts.

The city’s two airports cancelled a total of 943 flights because of the typhoon, cutting capacity by nearly 40 per cent, state broadcaster CCTV said.

Shanghai also suspended some metro lines on Monday, while China Railway Chengdu Group cancelled 115 trains, state news agency Xinhua reported.

Streets in the suburban districts of Jiading and Qingpu remained waterlogged, with residents sharing live-streams of the flooding on social media.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Dolphin had travelled 3,728 miles before making landfall, giving it a life cycle around three times longer than an ordinary typhoon and creating an “ultra-large” cloud system that enveloped eastern China.

The typhoon’s impact was also being compared with that of deadly Typhoon Doksuri, which battered China in 2023.

News.title: Burnham must show he has the spine to overrule Whitehall Blob that backs criminals, illegal migrants and the feckless
News.content:
Burnham v Blob

IT’S getting the right outcome that matters, so we welcome Andy Burnham’s belated determination to keep the killers of hero PC Andrew Harper behind bars.

We still don’t know how he’s going to do it — and nor does he, apparently. So nothing can be taken for granted.



But the penny finally appears to have dropped that it would be a disgusting insult to Andrew’s family and colleagues if remorseless thugs Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers walk free.

This does not forgive the confusion which has been sown. Indeed, Andrew’s grieving mum yesterday said the process had left her “twisted inside”.



First, Burnham ordered a review of Labour’s diabolical early release scheme when it emerged PC Harper’s killers would be included — raising hopes of an early U-turn.

Then, blindly taking the word of no-can-do officialdom, he last week concluded he would have to let them go after all — but wished he could do more.

Cue massive public outrage and nearly one million people signing a petition — which, by the way, is 40 TIMES more than have voted for our new Messiah-without-a-mandate PM.

Over the past seven days, Number Ten has lurched about calamitously as unaccountable Whitehall officials claimed it was all too difficult.

Just on Monday, Downing Street officially insisted it was “not possible” to exempt just one or two offenders.

Then, yesterday, came the collapse into basic moral decency and common sense, as Burnham said he was “increasingly confident” Cole and Bowers will now be kept locked up.



Which brings us to a wider, deeply worrying point.

Being PM — a job Burnham spent years plotting to get — is hard. It’s not enough to be affable and have a workable knowledge of pub snacks.

Many officials are utterly wet and useless. The State “Blob” will always take the side of criminals, illegal migrants, the feckless and the wokerati given half a chance.

Burnham needs to show he’s got the spine to order them to do the right thing at the FIRST time of asking. Is he up to it?

Trading insults

WHAT is Labour’s answer to the closure of 17,000 High Street shops this year?



Yes, rogue vape and barber shops are a blight. But what Andy Burnham fails to understand is that they only exist because criminal gangs have swooped to exploit Labour’s strangling of genuine retailers.

Business rates for independent stores have soared, while National Insurance and minimum wage rises make hiring staff impossibly expensive.

Ideologically driven parking charges and restrictions choke demand further.

Unless Burnham makes it easier for legitimate traders to survive, none of his tinkering will make any difference.

News.title: Terror trio including man who plotted to kidnap and behead soldier could be free within weeks
News.content:
THREE more dangerous Islamist terrorists — including one who planned to kidnap and behead a soldier — could be free within weeks after being granted parole hearings.

Parviz Khan, who got life with a minimum of 14 years in 2008 for the plot, has won a hearing on September 29, which could see him released.



His trial heard he was claiming £20,000 in benefits a year while planning to seize a British Muslim serviceman and decapitate him “like a pig”.

He was jailed alongside four others, but the Leicester crown court trial heard that he was the ringleader of the Birmingham-based cell.



Khan, 55, was denied parole in 2022 after a board said he was “not suitable” for release.

Rangzieb Ahmed, an al-Qaeda operative once dubbed Osama bin Laden’s right-hand man in Europe, has been granted a parole hearing on August 20.



He was jailed in 2008 for setting up a terrorist cell in Manchester and was the first person to be charged with directing terrorism in the UK.

His Manchester crown court trial heard he plotted mass murder, but he got a minimum term of just ten years.



Ahmed, 50, of Rochdale, was also denied parole in 2022, but has a new shot at freedom.

The third is Omar Khyam, of Crawley, West Sussex. He was part of an al-Qaeda cell that was jailed for plotting a series of attacks with fertiliser-based bombs.

Potential targets for “mass casualty” attacks included Bluewater shopping centre in Kent and London’s Ministry of Sound nightclub.

Khyam — linked to the July 7 London bombers — was jailed for conspiring to cause explosions, possessing 600kg of ammonium nitrate fertiliser for terrorism and possession of aluminium powder.

Cell ringleader Khyam was told he must serve at least 20 years at the Old Bailey in 2007.



A year later he was handed another four-year term for throwing boiling oil over another inmate at Frankland Prison, Co Durham.

Khyam, 45, is due before a panel for a hearing on December 2.

It comes after we told on Monday how an al-Qaeda trio who planned to blow up transatlantic planes could be freed.

Terrorists Waheed Zaman, Arafat Waheed Khan and Ibrahim Savant, all of London, were jailed in 2010.

Ghaffar Hussain, an expert on radicalisation and former counter-terror officer on the Government’s Prevent programme, said: “These people all present massive risks and this is extremely worrying.”



The Parole Board said: “Decisions are solely focused on what risk a prisoner could represent to the public if released and whether that risk is manageable.”

News.title: Fury as mega-dinghies capable of carrying up to 230 migrants brazenly offered for sale online
News.content:
MEGA-dinghies like the one which took a record 230 migrants to Britain are sold brazenly online by Chinese factories.

The Sun found a 49ft boat for £1,400 in just five minutes on the Alibaba marketplace website.



We told how a similar inflatable, packed with more passengers than carried by an easyJet Airbus, was escorted to Dover after leaving Berck, in Northern France, on Sunday night.

Sun analysis revealed the migrants on that one boat alone could cost British taxpayers up to £25million.



The dinghy we found was listed by Qingdao Rongsheng Sports Goods Co Ltd as a “fishing and cargo boat” in the “waterplay crafts” section of China’s largest online shopping site.

The firm can also provide an engine, or a sample dinghy with a one-year warranty for a cut-price £1,270.

They offer boats in sizes starting at 26ft and boast a rating of 4.8 out of 5.

Another seller we contacted, the Qingdao Jiahai Boat Co, provides a 32ft “sports yacht” for £860.

It said it would ship to European nations but, not did not reveal which ones.

The firm insisted: “Our vessels are used for transporting goods.”



Many mega-dinghies are exported through Turkey and Bulgaria to Germany, and then on to northern France.

Rob Bates, of the Centre for Migration Control, told The Sun: “The work of people smugglers has never been easier.

“The Home Office has failed to deter migrants making the crossing, and we will now see an armada of these readily-available vessels.”



Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “An industry facilitating Channel crossings has sprung up.

Illegal immigrants are finding new ways to cross, and the mega dinghies show how brazen this has become.”

French sea rescue charity SNSM said Monday’s boat had 260 people on board, but 30 were forced off because of the fear it would capsize.

Alibaba said: “We adhere to all applicable laws in the markets we operate in and require sellers to do the same.

“Listings for boats and dinghies on our platform are intended for legitimate commercial uses such as fishing, cargo transport and marine operations.”



A Government spokeswoman said: “We’re cracking down on these reckless and dangerous gangs – our work to disrupt their criminal supply chains has led to more than 1,100 small boats and engines seized since the election.

“There are also now more police on French beaches to intercept them before they set off.

“Small boat crossings are significantly down this year with the lowest number recorded for the month of July since 2020.”

A National Crime Agency spokesman told The Sun: “People smuggling gangs are constantly trying to adapt and we are working internationally to tackle their business models, end-to-end.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are proactively targeting and degrading the supply chain of boats and engines, the social media they use to advertise crossings, their finances, and the controlling minds coordinating the crossings, in the fight against organised immigration crime.”



Additional reporting: Julia Atherley

News.title: PM chairs emergency Cobra meeting as UK faces 'national emergency' over wildfires
News.content:
PM chairs emergency Cobra meeting as UK faces 'national emergency' over wildfires

Andy Burnham has convened an emergency Cobra meeting as the UK battles record-breaking heat, widespread wildfires and drought, with temperatures forecast to hit 38C this week

View 5 Images The Prime Minister will convene with ministers, officials and agencies as scorching temperatures persist across the UK (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/POOL PA via AP)

Andy Burnham will chair an emergency Cobra committee meeting on Wednesday in response to the sweltering heat, which has sparked widespread wildfires and plunged large swathes of the country into drought.

‌



The Prime Minister will convene with ministers, officials and agencies as scorching temperatures persist across the UK on Wednesday afternoon, with highs of 33C forecast, rising to as much as 38C on Thursday.

‌



Ministers from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the Home Office, and the Department for Health will be in attendance, alongside the Environment Agency.

‌



View 5 Images It will mark the second Cobra meeting this year dedicated to heatwaves, following a similar gathering during a period of high temperatures in June. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Child vanished at Maine beach because parent was too busy scrolling on phone READ MORE :

A Downing Street spokesperson confirmed the Government was aware that firefighters, farmers and NHS staff were all facing significant pressures linked to the extreme weather conditions.

On Tuesday, a firefighter union chief sounded the alarm, warning that the country is facing a "national emergency" amid the ongoing wildfire crisis.

‌



The Met Office has warned that the UK is on track for its hottest summer on record, as parts of the country brace for a fifth heatwave this season.

Rare amber "extreme heat" warnings have been issued by the forecaster for London and parts of the South East, East Midlands, East of England, West Midlands and South Yorkshire from 9am to midnight on Thursday.

The Government urged the public to keep a close eye on UK Health Security Agency heat health alerts, advising people to stay well hydrated and check in on family, friends and neighbours who may be particularly vulnerable.

‌



View 5 Images A major heathland blaze in the New Forest near Ringwood in Hampshire (Image: Forestry England/PA Wire)

A No 10 spokesperson said: "The Prime Minister will chair a meeting of COBR – the government emergency committee – this afternoon on the UK's ongoing response to extreme heat, wildfires and drought. We know how challenging this summer is proving, particularly for firefighters tackling wildfires, farmers working in drought conditions, and NHS staff in busy A&E units.

"We will continue to take the action needed to keep communities safe, protect water supplies and safeguard the environment."

‌



Met Office chief forecaster Chris Bulmer said: "While the peak heat will be more short-lived than recent heatwaves, temperatures widely into the mid-30s Celsius on Thursday brings the potential for impacts for some, which is why a Met Office warning has been issued.

"High pressure is now becoming dominant and temperatures will build day by day. Southerly and south-easterly winds will also tap into the hot conditions over Europe which helps develop this further notable heat in what has been a hot and dry summer so far for many in the south of the UK."

This comes as Steve Wright, general secretary of the Fire Brigades Union (FBU), cautioned that the UK is facing a national emergency "right now" with blazes breaking out across the country. Firefighters have tackled 966 wildfires across England and Wales this year, including 185 in the first 10 days of August alone, while July proved to be the busiest month on record for wildfires with 458 incidents, the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) revealed.

‌



Crews from Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service have been battling a blaze in the New Forest, which broke out after a van caught fire on the A31 near Ringwood on Sunday.

View 5 Images The Government confirmed it had announced £97 million in new funding to upgrade national firefighting capabilities, including off-road vehicles and specialist equipment. (Image: Getty Images)

The area affected by the fire is protected heathland and home to a number of rare species, according to the New Forest National Park Authority.

‌



Mr Wright told Times Radio: "In many parts of the country, firefighters do not have the new modern equipment to deal with these.

"They do not have the new modern personal protective equipment, the lightweight fire kit that we wear, the right helmets, lightweight helmets, breathable uniforms to make sure they're better protected, their health is protected when they're out dealing with these incidents for hours and hours on end."

Nearly three quarters of England and the whole of Wales are experiencing drought, after a record dry July and a very dry start to August combined with soaring temperatures have heaped pressure on water resources. Southern Water has lodged an application for a rare non-domestic drought order that would prohibit businesses from non-essential water usage, including washing cars and topping up swimming pools, warning that an "exceptional" shortage of rainfall has put supplies at risk across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.

‌



The water firm cautioned that 165,000 residents in the Southampton West supply area could face restricted access to water.

View 5 Images The Environment Agency revealed that 71.3% of England is now experiencing "flash drought", following a dry start to August after the country's driest July on record. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Environment Secretary Angela Eagle will rule on the application, which would mark the first such ban since May 2006.

Article continues below

Record-breaking heatwaves throughout May and June resulted in the deaths of more than 2,800 people, while swathes of the country were battered by further heatwaves last month as England and Wales endured their driest July since records began in 1836.

Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said: "I want to thank NHS staff who are once again stepping up to cope with the extra pressures that hot weather brings.

"Extreme heat can be dangerous, so staying aware of warnings and alerts in place can make a real difference."

News.title: Ohio lightning strike: 16 inmates hit outside Ohio prison
News.content:
Ohio lightning strike: 16 inmates hit outside Ohio prison

Just before 6pm local time ambulances from Lorain, Medina and Cuyahoga counties were dispatched to the Grafton Correction Institution after lightning sttic

View 2 Images Fire crews at the scene of the Ohio prison

At least 16 inmates were struck by lightning outside a correctional facility in Ohio, authorities said.

‌



Just before 6pm local time ambulances from Lorain, Medina and Cuyahoga counties were dispatched to the Grafton Correction Institution.

‌



A spokesperson for Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction said: "Initial reports indicate a lightning strike occurred this evening while incarcerated individuals were returning from the evening meal.

‌



View 2 Images Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction

"At this time, 16 individuals are being transported to an outside hospital for treatment, including one individual who was life-flighted. There have been no reported deaths at this time. We are continuing to assess and monitor the situation."

‌



Officials said the inmates were leaving one building and heading to another after a meal when they were struck.

All were transported to local hospitals with non-life-threatening injuries although some of the patients were described as being critically hurt.

It came after Ohio was battered by powerful storms that flooded parts of the state with several feet of water killing at least one person.
