News.title: Mum who vanished from Birmingham with three kids may be 117 miles away - police say
News.content:
Mum who vanished from Birmingham with three kids may be 117 miles away - police say

Police have issued an update in the search for missing Alimat and her three children who were all last seen on Saturday in the Digbeth area of central Birmingham

View 2 Images Police are looking to find Alimat and her three children

West Midlands Police have issued an update in their search for a missing mum and her three children.

‌



Alimat, 31, from Wolverhampton, was last seen on Saturday with her children in the Digbeth area of central Birmingham. As per shots taken from CCTV footage, the 31-year-old was spotted on security cameras walking with her three children and at least two suitcases.

‌



She was also pushing along a pram which, as well carrying her smallest child, appeared to be rammed full of clothes and coats.

‌



View 2 Images London Euston railway station (Image: Getty)

As per the Birmingham Live, the Wolverhampton mum and her kids have not been seen since. West Midlands Police took to social media, posting: "Have you seen Alimat?". "The 31-year-old from Wolverhampton is missing along with her three children.", Click here to 

In an update yesterday West Midlands Poice believed they could have travelled 117 miles away from New Street station to London Euston.

‌



A spokesperson said: "We are continuing to ask for your help to locate Alimat who is missing from #Wolverhampton. The 31-year-old, and her three children, were last seen in the city on Saturday before being spotted in #Birmingham city centre the following day.

"It is understood she may have travelled from New Street station to London Euston. If you can help, please call 999 quoting PID 461858."

Of the 170,000 people who go missing in the UK each year, some cases remain etched in our minds, while others fade too quickly from public attention, if they were ever known at all.

‌



Yet for the families and friends of those still missing, the need for answers and support never diminishes as hours, days, months, and years pass by.

This is why, in 2025, the Mirror is launching Missed . In partnership with Missing People, our mission is to bring awareness to every publicly listed missing person in the UK through our live, interactive map.

Article continues below

Simply zoom into your chosen area to see how many people have gone missing in that location. Zoom in further to reveal photos of missing persons plus the names, ages and length of time they’ve been missing.

Simple to use, the map allows you to report a sighting in confidence as well as share on social media.

For advice, support and options, if you or someone you love goes missing, text or call Missing People’s Helpline on 116 000 or email 116000@missingpeople.org.uk. It’s free, confidential and non-judgmental, and sightings information can also be taken. Or visit www.missingpeople.org.uk

News.title: Thousands to get money off electricity bills for living near pylons
News.content:
Thousands to get money off electricity bills for living near pylons

The first wave of projects include National Grid transmission infrastructure from Bramford to Twinstead in East Anglia, the North London Reinforcement project and the Emmock substation in north east Scotland

View 2 Images Thousands could be set for cheaper bills (Image: Getty)

Thousands of households living near new or upgraded pylons will be the first to get money off their electricity bills, the government has announced.

‌



Payments will start from next year, as the first projects expected to qualify for a new bill discount scheme are unveiled.

‌



Communities in over 40 locations will get direct benefits for hosting vital infrastructure that will provide cheaper, clean electricity to the whole country. Those living within 500 metres of the projects could get get £2,500 off their electricity bills over 10 years.

‌



The first wave of projects include National Grid transmission infrastructure from Bramford to Twinstead in East Anglia, the North London Reinforcement project and the Emmock substation in north east Scotland.

How to save water and money with more than two-thirds of England now in drought READ MORE :

View 2 Images Energy Minister Michael Shanks said upgrading Britain's electricity grid was 'vital' (Image: Joseph Raynor/ Reach PLC)

Energy Minister Michael Shanks said: “Upgrading Britain’s electricity grid is a vital part of how we deliver secure, homegrown energy and unlock economic growth across the country.

‌



“It is a moment of national renewal – upgrading what was built largely in the 1960s for the modern age and is our route to bringing down electricity bills for households across the country.

“It’s vital we build again as a country and we are determined those communities which host pylons should benefit, which is why we’re bringing down the energy bills of those hosting this vital national infrastructure.”

A Government impact assessment earlier this year found that more than 100,000 households could benefit from the scheme in the coming decades as further projects follow.

‌



Most households that qualify for the scheme will receive the discount automatically on their electricity bill every six months via their energy supplier, officials said, although some may need to apply, such as those on commercial meters.

Ministers said they will be directly contacted by their energy supplier or Ofgem with further information in the first half of 2027.

Neil Lawrence, Ofgem executive director for delivery and schemes, said: “Communities that host new electricity transmission infrastructure are playing a vital role in delivering the cleaner, more secure energy system Britain needs.

Article continues below

“The bill discount scheme will help ensure eligible households living near these projects see a direct benefit through discounts on their energy bills. As the scheme administrator, Ofgem’s role is to make sure payments are delivered effectively, fairly and transparently to eligible customers.”

News.title: Tributes pour in for woman, 23, who died at scene of crash which claimed two lives
News.content:
Tributes pour in for woman, 23, who died at scene of crash which claimed two lives

Natasha Denman, 23, was one of two people in their 20s who sadly died at the scene of a serious crash as her family express their 'heartbreak' over her 'sudden' passing

View 2 Images Natasha Denman, 23, died in the crash in Gorton (Image: GMP)

Tributes are pouring in for a 'funny' and 'caring' 23-year-old who lost her life alongside a 24-year-old man in a horrific crash in Manchester last week.

Natasha Denman, 23, was one of two people in their 20s who sadly died at the scene of a collision on Hyde Road in Gorton on Wednesday evening (August 5).

Her family have been left 'heartbroken' following her 'sudden' passing after the car she was travelling in collided with a stationary digger near the junction with Clumber Road at around 9:30pm.

Greater Manchester Police said that four people were in the car, with Natasha and Jack Cartwright, 24, passing away at the scene.

Ms Denman's family paid tribute to their 'loving and caring' Tasha on August 11, expressing their 'heartbreak'.

View 2 Images A Greater Manchester Police vehicle (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News)

Her family said: “Tasha was a much-loved daughter, sister, granddaughter, niece and cousin. We, as a family, will never recover from her sudden and unexpected passing at such a young age.

“Our hearts are forever broken. We would like her to be remembered as the naturally funny, loving and caring person she was.

“She can rest peacefully knowing she will always be cherished. We would politely ask people to accept our request for privacy at this time.”

Apollo Simms, 26, of Tealby Road, Manchester, has been charged with two counts of death by dangerous driving and failing to provide a sample for analysis in relation to the incident. He was due to appear at Manchester Magistrates' Court on August 11.

Police confirmed another man who was arrested has been released on bail.

The force are appealing for any witnesses who may have seen the moments prior to the collision or anyone who has mobile phone, ring doorbell or dash cam footage to get in contact with them to assist the investigation.

Article continues below

Anyone with information can contact police on 0161 856 4741 quoting the log number 3717 of 05/08/2026. Alternatively, contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Ferry capsizes leaving 15 dead and more missing on world's largest man-made lake in Zimbabwe
News.content:
Ferry capsizes leaving 15 dead and more missing on world's largest man-made lake in Zimbabwe

Search and rescue operations were deployed on the huge lake which is teeming with Nile crocodiles and hippopotamuses - there were 114 adult passengers onboard at the time

View 3 Images A ferry has capsized in Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba (Image: Mutsa Murombedzi/X)

A ferry has capsized in Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba, leaving 15 people dead and 27 other missing.

‌



The country's national disaster management agency said 77 people were rescued after the incident on Tuesday, August 11 and made it to a small island on the lake, with boats now being dispatched to bring the survivors back.

‌



The boat has a carrying capacity of 90 people. Zimbabwe's Civil Protection Unit said it could only confirm through registered ticket sales that there were 114 adult passengers onboard, with five crew members.

‌



There could have been an unknown number of children below ticketing age who were not accounted for.

Zimbabwean state broadcaster ZBC published video of speedboats making their way to what appeared to be an overturned boat on the lake as a helicopter hovered overhead.

View 3 Images The boat had a carrying capacity of 90 people (Image: ZBC News)

‌



An underwater team for search and rescue operations was deployed on the lake, which forms part of the border between Zimbabwe and neighbouring Zambia.

Lake Kariba is the largest man-made lake in the world by volume. It was created by building a dam wall to block the Zambezi River, resulting in a valley slowly filling with water to form a huge lake.

The lake is teeming with Nile crocodiles and hippopotamuses.

‌



View 3 Images There could have been an unknown number of children below ticketing age who were on board (Image: Mutsa Murombedzi/X)

Mutsa Murombedzi, a local member of Parliament, said rural communities use the boat to travel along the lake to the town of Kariba, a journey that usually takes about five hours.

Ms Murombedzi posted a video of what she said were people on shore waving off what appeared to be the ageing ferry at the start of its journey.

Article continues below

Some people standing on the shore were worried the ferry would not survive strong waves on the lake, according to the video.

News.title: Police make major breakthrough after 85-year-old grandad 'kidnapped in error'
News.content:
Police make major breakthrough after 85-year-old grandad 'kidnapped in error'

Detectives found a body 11 days after the 85-year-old was snatched from his bed in a shock case of mistaken identity - but now, police have a fresh update on the case

View 4 Images Chris Baghsarian was kidnapped from his home in Australia

Police have made a breakthrough in horror case of mistaken identity, in which an 85-year-old grandfather was allegedly kidnapped and murdered by masked bandits.

Sydney pensioner Chris Baghsarian made international headlines earlier this year when elderly man was kidnapped from his north Sydney home by masked assailants at about 5am on February 13.

New South Wales Police later revealed the pensioner was likely taken by mistake, with detectives and family urging the widower's kidnappers to return him to them safe and sound. The 85-year-old's body was found 12 days later, nearly 30 miles from where he was last seen alive.

But now, Australian detectives from the Robbery and Serious Crime Squad have revealed fresh charges have been laid in connection to Mr Baghsarian's alleged kidnapping and murder.

View 4 Images Police say Chris Baghsarian, 85, was kidnapped by mistake (Image: NSW POLICE)

According to NSW Police: "Following further inquiries, at about 10.40am yesterday (August 11), strike force detectives – with assistance from Northwest Metropolitan Operations Support Group – arrested a 51-year-old woman in Lethbridge Park [29 miles from Sydney's city centre].

"She was taken to Mt Druitt Police Station, where she was charged with accessory after the fact to murder."

View 4 Images Police make an arrest in an investigation into the murder of 85-year-old grandfather Chris Baghsarian. (Image: NSW POLICE)

Police added that the 51-year-old woman has since been refused bail and is set to appear in Western Sydney at Mt Druitt Local Court on Wednesday (August 12).

She now joins 11 others who have also been charged in the wake of Mr Baghsarian's death, following subsequent investigations into his alleged abduction and murder.

These latest charges come five months on from that tragic day that Mr Baghsarian initially vanished, with his family, police, and even the state premier for New South Wales all issuing pleas to his alleged captors to beg for the pensioner's safe return.

Grainy vision also aired on Australian news channel Nine, which showed two men — one wearing a high-visibility jacket — arriving at the elderly man's North Ryde home in a dark four-wheel-drive. They were seen on CCTV before dark, approaching the property.

Mere moments later, Mr Baghsarian can be seen being pushed and shoved inside the vehicle - the last time he would be seen alive - with the car then speeding away into the darkness.

View 4 Images Mr Baghsarian was pushed into a waiting car as per grainy CCTV footage aired on Aussie TV (Image: Nine)

Police later discovered an abandoned dark Toyota SUV that they believed was linked to the abduction. The car, found more than eight miles away, was completely burned out.

New South Wales Police Detective Acting Superintendent Andrew Marks said at the time officers were “a million per cent confident” the kidnappers had taken the wrong man, stressing that Mr Baghsarian and his family had no links to organised crime.

New South Wales premier Chris Minns described the family as “distraught” in the days following his adduction. He too had called on those responsible for the savage abduction to do the right thing. “This is a man over 80 years old,” Mr Minns said. “Please return him to his family."

But, their pleas ultimately fell on deaf ears, with the sad tale coming to an end the village of Pitt Town, a regional community 40 miles north-east of Sydney.

Article continues below

Later that month, NSW police detectives stormed the homes of Gerard Andrews, 29, and Daniel Stevens, 24, with the pair the first two to be charged with the murder and abduction of Mr Baghsarian.

Andrews was caught so off guard he was barely dressed when police dragged him out onto the street, with his trousers falling down around his ankles as he was he was frogmarched to a police car by cops.

News.title: Major UK river turns 'milky green' after mysterious white liquid dumped into water
News.content:
Major UK river turns 'milky green' after mysterious white liquid dumped into water

The River Irwell has turned a strange shade of green as it passes through Radcliffe, in Greater Manchester with one local official blaming the colour change on an “organised dump” of a milky white substance into the waterway.

View 3 Images The river has turned a milky green colour (Image: Councillor Ken Simpson)

A UK river has turned a vivid shade of 'milky green' after being polluted by large quantities of an unidentified substance over the weekend.

‌



The River Irwell turned the unusual shade after it passed through Radcliffe, in Greater Manchester, pictures from this weekend show.

‌



The contamination spread downstream in large quantities according to snaps shared on Saturday, the Manchester Evening News reports.

‌



Local councillor Ken Simpson, who represents the Radcliffe East ward, said he suspected the colour change was due to an “organised dump” because of the “sheer quantity” of the substance.

The Environment Agency said it is investigating the source of the leak and has “taken samples for analysis”. United Utilities, which is responsible for water and waste water services in the region, has confirmed that the spill did not come from its network.

View 3 Images Some locals blame intentional 'dumping' (Image: Councillor Ken Simpson)

‌



Councillor Simpson, who is a member of the Radcliffe First party on Bury council, reported there was “no strong chemical smell" in the area, saying a senior United Utilities officer called out to the site “suspected it could be a waste milk dump”.

“I’ve just been to the location of what appears to be a spillage of an unidentified substance into the River Irwell alongside the new footbridge on Rectory Lane,” he said. “United Utilities are on scene but have already confirmed it isn’t one of their outlets but a private drain from one of Radcliffe's ancient “goits” which now run beneath local housing.

“Due to the sheer quantity of whatever this substance is and that we have had reports of it increasing and decreasing at different times of day it appears to be an organised dump of some kind.

‌



“The spillage has immediately diffused into the downstream river completely changing its colour to a milky green colour," he added. "I know this is obvious but my advice is to keep children and pets out of the water downstream until we have confirmation it is safe.”

Residents say this is not the first time unidentified substances have contaminated the waters in that area. One person said spills "happen a lot there", adding this incident "looked very big".

View 3 Images The Environment Agency said it has taken samples (Image: Councillor Ken Simpson)

‌



Another added: “It’s just awful, even if it’s ‘just’ milk it will have a massive impact and strip the affected area of oxygen. Britain's rivers are in a terrible state.”

The Environment Agency confirmed it received a report of a similar incident last month.

A spokesman for the organisation said: “We take our role in cleaning up our rivers, lakes and seas seriously. We are investigating the source of this white substance and have also taken samples for analysis.

Article continues below

“Any suspected pollution incidents should be reported as soon as possible to our 24/7 hotline on 0800 80 70 60, or online.”

A United Utilities spokesman said: “Following reports of pollution in the River Irwell in Radcliffe on Saturday, our teams inspected our assets and confirmed the substance was not linked to our network.”

News.title: 'Overwhelmed' probation officers warn  of early prison release crime risk
News.content:
The chief inspector of probation for England and Wales has told the BBC the early release of thousands of prisoners could lead to "a serious sexual or violent offence or even murder" because of the demands on probation staff to monitor offenders.

The government is set to release 5,000 offenders from October as part of new laws to create more space in overcrowded prisons.

Probation officers supervise offenders after prison sentences and check they follow the terms of their release, such as sticking to curfews and not taking drugs.

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said "protecting the public is our top priority", adding it had invested in probation and hiring trainee officers.

But Martin Jones, His Majesty's Chief Inspector of probation for England and Wales, told the BBC that "ultimately I'm not fully confident that the probation system will be able to cope with this massive work and there's a risk that things will go wrong".

"Probation services are already under unprecedented pressure.

"I mean, they're managing a caseload of 258,000 cases, that's nearly three times the number that are in our prisons, and obviously the early release scheme will be increasing that pressure considerably."

Probation officers help former prisoners with housing, employment and access to benefits once in the community, and help protect the public by assessing the risk of further offending.

Their workload will increase substantially when more offenders - some of whom will have been convicted of violent offences - will be released months earlier than planned as part of the Sentencing Act.

According to the chief inspector, probation caseload has increased by 8% over the last two years.

Much of that is down to a separate early release scheme which was implemented in 2024 after prisons nearly reached full capacity.

That scheme has led to tens of thousands of offenders being let out sooner.

When asked what risk the additional early releases due to start in the autumn could pose to the public, Jones said "that could be a serious sexual or violent offence or even murder".

One probation officer told the BBC the upcoming releases had put him and his colleagues into "a state of panic".

"We can't cope with this - we've been saying that to anybody who will listen.

"At the minute I think it's pure panic in terms of where we're at. I don't understand how there can be this level of pressure put on us.

"The worst that can happen is that things are missed, plans aren't put into place and we don't give people the level of service they need and that leads to serious further offences.

"That leads to death under supervision."

In a statement, an MoJ spokesperson said the department had exceeded its recruitment target for last year, with 1,389 trainee probation officers starting.

The spokesperson said this is "making sure the Probation Service has the resource it needs to keep dangerous offenders under closer surveillance than ever before".

"The Sentencing Act is restoring order to a prison system left on the brink of collapse, while our record Â£700m investment in probation and community punishment is ensuring staff have the resources, powers, and technology they need to manage offenders safely in the community," the spokesperson added.

News.title: Woman assaulted by double murderer says nightmare became 'real life' when police let him attack again
News.content:
A woman who was attacked by double murderer Simon Levy eight years ago has told the BBC the police made her nightmare "real life" by letting him go on to kill and attack more women.

Laura, whose surname we are not using, said she had been trying to protect other women by reporting Levy in 2018, but feels betrayed by what he was later allowed to do after being released from jail.

Levy was convicted on Friday of murdering Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo and Sheryl Wilkins and raping another woman in London in 2025. He will be sentenced on Wednesday.

He was also convicted earlier this year of sexually assaulting 11 other women, 10 of them on trains and the Tube in London between 2023 and 2025.

Police, prosecutors and the courts made a series of disastrous decisions that left Levy free. He attacked 14 more women before being taken off the streets, despite being a sex offender who was monitored by the Met Police.

Levy was a registered sex offender because he sexually assaulted Laura â and a separate victim - in summer 2018.

Laura says that Levy is "evil" and that his attack "completely changed my life".

But she now realises that what she would "think about, dream about, have nightmares about was actually happening - he was actually still out preying on vulnerable women".

Waiving her anonymity, she said she had been trying to protect other women by ensuring that Levy was jailed.

"I feel like when I reported it, I was doing the right thing and I thought I was doing it to protect other women.

"I feel absolutely devastated for all of those women that have been affected by him â and the families."

Laura says she feels let down by the whole criminal justice system including the Met Police, the courts and judges who bailed Levy, as well as the Crown Prosecution Service.

"They're all as guilty for allowing him to continue to do what he was doing", she says.

"They could have prevented so many women from being hurt.

"They could have prevented two women from losing their lives."

News.title: UK to get best eclipse since 1999 as Moon blocks out Sun across Europe
News.content:
But when it comes to the weather, fortunes will be mixed. In much of the UK, clear skies should give many a good view of the eclipse. However, across some parts of north Wales, northern England and especially Scotland and Northern Ireland, areas of cloud could move in between 18:00 and 19:00.

Across some parts of western Scotland and in towards the north and west of Northern Ireland, cloud could bring outbreaks of rain.

For those lucky enough to be in Spain, there will be clear skies for people to see a total eclipse in Bilbao, Valencia and Palma, Mallorca, while both Barcelona and Madrid will see more than 99% coverage.

Depending on the location, the total eclipse will peak between 20:26 and 20:33 local time (19:26 to 19:33 BST).

Crowds have been flocking from all over the world to northern Spain for the event with half a million visitors expected, according to the finance ministry.

Julie who travelled with her family from Brest, France, to the Spanish city of Burgos, said she was "very excited".

"We came from very far to see it in totality. I have seen [it] once and it was beautiful and amazing - I am so happy to have the chance to see one again."

Leonor Aguilar from JaÃ©n, Spain, said: "During that minute and a half, what I hope to see is the grandeur of nature and to experience it with my family.

"We often spend money on trivial things instead of investing in something as beautiful as witnessing such a marvellous sight."

Martin Griffith, the director of Brecon Beacons Observatory, in Wales, described the eclipse as "one of the great phenomena of nature".

"It is going to be a fantastic eclipse in Spain, we are right on the path of totality," he said. "What they will see is about a minute and 40 seconds of totality. It will be dark, the Moon will completely cover the Sun.

"Although we know they happen quite often we're not always in the path of totality - they could be over the Pacific Ocean, but to have it over land is just incredible," he said.

The next time the Moon obscures as much of the Sun on the British Isles will be in 2081, and the next total solar eclipse in the UK will be in 2090.

News.title: Three ways to watch the solar eclipse safely without glasses
News.content:
With some online orders not able to arrive until the end of the week and shops running out of stock, it may be too late to buy eclipse glasses in time for Wednesday.

But you can still safely watch the spectacle using some household items.

People in the UK will see a partial eclipse - rather than the total eclipse that will be seen in parts of Spain, Greenland and Iceland - but it is the country's most significant eclipse since 1999.

Experts say enthusiasts should not to look directly at the Sun without specialist glasses.

And you shouldn't be tempted to try using sunglasses or dark goggles instead.

They often don't give enough UV protection when looking directly at the Sun and you could end up seriously damaging your eyesight, according to The Royal Astronomical Society.

Here are some viewing methods to try instead.

News.title: Burnham to chair Cobra meeting on extreme heat as temperatures surge again
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham will chair a meeting of the government's emergency Cobra committee on Wednesday to discuss the UK's response to the extreme heat, as temperatures are set to soar again.

A No 10 spokesperson said the government understood firefighters, farmers and NHS staff were all facing challenges connected to the weather.

It comes as the record for the number of days reaching 30C in any year in the UK has been broken, according to the Met Office.

After several locations exceeded 30C on Sunday, there have now been a total of 35 days where the maximum daily temperature has exceeded this threshold - beating the 34 days set in 1995.

This tally is expected to be topped again on Wednesday and Thursday with temperatures peaking in the mid-to-high 30s across the Midlands and south-east of England - and the Met Office has issued a rare amber extreme heat warning, external for Thursday, when 38C is possible.

News.title: Military still risks failing victims, review finds
News.content:
A leaked internal Ministry of Defence (MoD) report, obtained by the BBC, has highlighted serious failings in a new military command set up to investigate the most severe crimes, including rape and sexual assault.

The Defence Serious Crime Command (DSCC) was launched after the death of 19-year-old Gunner Jaysley Beck. An inquest later found the Army's mishandling of sexual assault and harassment complaints made by Beck contributed to her taking her own life, and exposed "systemic failings".

However, an internal review has highlighted continued concerns with the unit and warned the military still risks failing victims.

The MoD said the review's findings had been accepted and significant work has been undertaken since.

The DSCC was created in 2022 to investigate serious crimes independently, outside the military's chain of command.

However, the BBC can reveal that an internal review, which was carried out between 21 August 2025 and 12 November 2025 and overseen by a former senior civilian police officer, concluded that if the DSCC was subjected to scrutiny similar to civilian police forces there would be "a significant risk of (it) being graded as inadequate".

In a statement, the MoD said the review was commissioned "to provide honest challenge, identify areas of improvement and to help ensure the highest standards for victims and witnesses".

It added that following the findings, the DSCC had carried out significant work "including further investment in victim and witness support, strengthening governance and safeguarding arrangements and accrediting investigators to nationally recognised policing standards".

The DSCC was committed to transparency, continuous improvement and ensuring victims receive the support and service they deserve, the statement continued.

News.title: PM admits cost of living help is not enough and hints at further support
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he accepts his announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.

Burnham told BBC's Wake up to Money he will deliver an "accumulation of smaller things" that "combine to take the pressure down" on household budgets.

He spoke of an overhaul of train fares and "more public control" of energy, water and housing but did not give details on how he would bring this about.

Burnham has made a number of announcements to help people with the cost of living since taking office, including the removal of VAT from domestic electricity bills and bringing forward an already planned end to 'subscription traps'.

Asked whether the changes he had announced were not significant to people struggling, he said: "I can accept criticism that this isn't enough, because I wouldn't say it's enough.

"But I take an approach to politics where I do what I can, when I can. Just take that little bit of pressure off and address an issue that you know needs addressing.

"It's not the end of the story," he added.

The prime minister, who is embarking on a tour of the UK while Parliament is in recess, said he believed "more public control of essential services" such as water, energy and housing, "would mean we could get to a more substantial answer to the cost of living crisis".

On water, he said it would not be easy to reverse the privatisation of water companies in England and Wales that took place in the 1980s.

"But very much, I'm looking at what can be done. Same with energy."

He also said that, following the return of rail operators to public ownership, he wanted to "remodel the rail fares so that we can get more public benefit for people".

It comes as the government said on Wednesday that people living within 1,600ft (500m) of new upgraded electricity pylons and substations across Britain will receive a Â£250 annual discount on their bills for a decade.

Burnham told the BBC he has asked Chancellor John Healey to look at what the government can do further on the cost of living in the upcoming Budget, on 28 October, and that Healey has said it will be his "main focus".

Healey has made it clear he will oversee "strong fiscal discipline" â which will limit how much the government has to spend.

One major think tank recently warned that he will have to raise taxes or cut spending to meet Burnham's pledges on defence and the cost of living.

Labour's manifesto pledge was to not increase taxes for working people â including income tax, VAT and National Insurance Contributions (NICs) - which Burnham has said he will uphold.

He will likely face pressure to address rising costs for businesses, after previous budgets under Rachel Reeves saw employer's national insurance and minimum wages go up.

Last month Burnham said pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England would be given a 20% cut to business rates from April, calling it a "first step" to help the industry.

He told the BBC he accepted the national insurance hike had added pressure on businesses, and that the government would look at business rates "more broadly".

Burnham said: "I would like to bring down the cost of doing businesses. I want to make high streets more vibrant across the country. I know that cannot be done by simply wishing it."

But he said he did not want to "at this point, start making commitments".

"Those are for the Budget."

News.title: Fifty police chiefs call for PM to prevent early release of PC Harper's killers
News.content:
The police chiefs from Scotland, England, Wales and Northern Ireland also called for greater consideration of victims when prisoners have their sentences altered - such as with the government's early release scheme, which was designed to reduce prison overcrowding.

Under changes to the Sentencing Act made this year, Cole and Bowers, who were sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter in 2020, will become eligible for release from custody after serving half of their sentences.

In the letter, released on Tuesday evening, police chiefs said the early release of PC Harper's killers, and that of anyone involved in the death of an officer, could cast doubt over the "value placed on their service and sacrifice when they put themselves in harm's way to protect others".

They outlined three requests of the prime minister, beginning with pursuing "every lawful option to determine whether the earlier release of those responsible for PC Andrew Harper's death can be prevented" - which Burnham has already pledged to do.

Second, they called on the government to put greater consideration into the crimes committed by prisoners when altering their sentences.

They wrote: "Where an offender has caused a death, committed exceptionally serious violence, or presents an ongoing risk to individuals or communities, there should be explicit consideration of public protection, victim impact and community safety before release arrangements are amended.

"This is not simply a question of punishment. It is a question of ensuring that public protection, victim confidence and community safety remain central to decisions that may substantially reduce the time an offender spends in custody."

Lastly, the letter called for victims and bereaved families to be "properly considered whenever significant changes are made to sentencing or release arrangements".

Around 5,000 people are expected to be released under the early release scheme, down from 6,000 after exemptions were previously announced for those convicted of the most serious crimes including rape, child sex offences and grooming.

News.title: First 'pounds for pylons' energy bill discount sites revealed
News.content:
The first locations where households living close to new upgraded electricity pylons and substations will receive a Â£250 annual discount on their bills have been revealed.

Customers living within 1,600ft (500m) of 43 transmission projects across Britain will be eligible for the payments for up to 10 years under the bill discount scheme, sometimes dubbed "pounds for pylons".

UK ministers say replacing and upgrading decades-old infrastructure is vital for distributing renewable power and improving energy security.

Critics, however, argue the discounts are meagre compensation for the impact on their homes, neighbourhoods, and the environment.

About two-thirds of the projects are in Scotland, to support the fast-growing wind energy sector.

But major upgrades are also planned across Britain, including areas north of London, as well as East Anglia, the Midlands, and North Wales.

News.title: Children as young as nine hurt in growing number of e-scooter crashes
News.content:
Most of the incidents in Manchester, Liverpool and Sheffield involved private e-scooters, often on public roads, pavements or footpaths, despite that being illegal.

Private e-scooters are meant only for use on private land, with the owner's permission.

Half of the children injured were aged between 10 and 13. Nearly two-thirds were boys.

Most injuries were sustained by the rider - only 5% were pedestrians that had been hit by an e-scooter - and the most common cause was falling off the e-scooter.

Around 11% were collisions with a vehicle, which was often linked to more serious injuries.

Injuries to the arms and legs were the most common, followed by head or facial injuries.

The doctors say tougher laws are urgently needed. Helmet use is not mandatory in the UK, unlike some other countries.

Some have described the private e-scooter situation in the UK as the "Wild West" with few following any rules.

The researchers told the Emergency Medicine Journal that schools, local councils, youth groups and road safety campaigns all have a role to play.

"Clearly, reporting these accidents is important to influence and change policy, but there must also be an onus on retailers to clearly advise customers of the law, and policymakers to regulate private e-scooters, such as with speed limiters, or mandate helmet use," they say.

To legally rent an e-scooter in the UK, which can be used on roads and cycle lanes, you must be at least 16 and hold a full or provisional driving licence, and the rental company must provide appropriate insurance. Rental e-scooters typically have a limited top speed of around 15mph.

A Department for Transport spokesperson said: "These are concerning findings, and our thoughts are with anyone who has been injured on our roads.

"It is illegal for private e-scooters to be used on roads, pavements or in other public spaces, including by under 16s, and we're bringing forward new laws to make their use safe and legal, including consulting on requirements like helmets."

News.title: Criticism as thousands of seats empty at Europeans Athletics Championships
News.content:
Nearly 10,000 seats were empty at Birmingham's Alexander Stadium for the European Athletics Championships on Monday evening.

A crowd of 13,623 watched as Britain's 24-year-old sprinter Amy Hunt stormed to her first senior international title, in a stadium that has a capacity of 23,000.

Athletics supporters blamed ticket prices, with some describing them as "extortionate", while BBC commentator Steve Cram commented that spectator numbers were a "little disappointing".

But Birmingham 2026 organisers said they were "delighted" with ticket sales, which have "far surpassed" their targets with "Friday, Saturday and Sunday evening sessions approaching sell-out, with several other sessions close to capacity".

On Monday, Category A tickets for the home straight cost Â£150 with no concessions for juniors.

For the men's 100m final on Tuesday, those same seats cost Â£110, again with no concessions - while a similar ticket for the same final in Rome two years ago was 88 euros (Â£75).

It is Britain's first time hosting the championships in their 92-year history.

News.title: Wealthier areas must play their part in housing asylum seekers, Burnham suggests
News.content:
Labour has pledged to stop using asylum hotels, a costly form of accommodation that has become a focal point for anti-migrant protests.

The government has sought to house migrants at military sites across the country instead, announcing in June that it planned to open three more including the site in Bicester, Oxfordshire.

The plans have prompted protests there, with residents of nearby Piddington voting to stage a symbolic referendum on leaving the UK.

Burnham said on Tuesday that he would listen to and address the concerns being raised.

"I don't know the issue yet in detail, but in some ways, as I understand it, it is about creating secure space," he said.

"We understand people's concerns and I will look into the issues raised by the good people of Piddington."

But he added: "I do believe all parts of the country need to work, to play their part."

After winning the Makerfield by-election in June, Burnham promised to end "HMO Britain" and said he would change Britain's asylum accommodation system.

HMOs, or houses in multiple occupation, have been widely used by government contractors to house asylum seekers, often in lower income, urban areas.

Last week, there were anti-immigration demonstrations in the town of Thetford, Norfolk, with protesters attempting to enter homes where they believed asylum seekers were living.

In response to Burnham's interview, Philp reiterated the Conservatives' policy of leaving the European Convention on Human Rights in order to deport migrants to their country of origin or a safe third country.

"Andy Burnham just doesn't get it," he wrote on X.

"Illegal immigrants should all be deported within a week of arrival - to their country of origin or a safe third country like Rwanda."

Government statistics, external showed there were 97,519 people in receipt of asylum support at the end of March, with 20,885 in hotel accommodation.

The figures added that 72,768 people were in other accommodation, including "dispersal accommodation" - which normally means houses in the community.

The remaining 3,866 people were in receipt of subsistence support only, according to the government.

The regions and nations with the highest number of asylum seekers in receipt of Home Office support included 19,578 in the north-west of England, 13,687 in London, 11,969 in the West Midlands and 8,635 in Yorkshire and the Humber.

The Home Office said the regions with the most supported asylum seekers as a proportion of their overall population were the north-east and north-west of England, with 26 and 25 supported people per 10,000 residents respectively.

It added the local authorities with the highest numbers of supported asylum seekers within them were Glasgow city (3,870), Birmingham (2,142), Liverpool (2,053), Coventry (1,712) and Belfast (1,607).

Burnham, during his time serving as the mayor of Greater Manchester, threatened to block the region from housing any more asylum seekers in 2018.

He complained about the government's dispersal system and said Greater Manchester's public services could not continue to support "disproportionate" numbers of people compared with elsewhere in the country.

Burnham at the time said the north-west of England was hosting 25% of the national population of asylum applicants who require housing and support - with Greater Manchester housing 70% of the region's numbers.

The then-Home Secretary Sajid Javid replied by promising to work towards a fairer distribution.

News.title: Man guilty of harassing MP Stella Creasy on Tube train
News.content:
A 63-year-old man has been found guilty of harassing the Labour MP for Walthamstow after preventing her from leaving a Tube carriage and behaving in an "abusive and aggressive" manner.

Clifford Wilby, from east London, targeted Stella Creasy on a Victoria line train between Walthamstow Central and Finsbury Park on 15 July last year.

Westminster Magistrates' Court heard how Wilby spoke to Creasy about knife crime and her "failings as a Member of Parliament" before filming her, leading to members of the public intervening.

Deputy Chief Magistrate Tan Ikram found Wilby guilty of using threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour with intent to cause harassment, alarm or distress.

Wilby and Creasy first met during a Zoom meeting in 2024 as part of her role as an MP.

She said he started to make a complaint about a constituent and she reminded him that she could not discuss somebody else's case.

Creasy said he had "made a series of very serious allegations", became abusive and "referred to the fact he had been diagnosed as a psychopath".

The meeting was stopped because of Wilby's behaviour.

News.title: Councils to get more powers to stop vape and betting shops, PM announces
News.content:
New vape shops will require planning permission and councils will get more powers to block new betting shops, under government plans aimed at improving high streets.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said town centres had been "hollowed out" by decades of decline and for many people, the high streets they grew up with are "unrecognisable".

He said the plans were "shaped" by a series of BBC News investigations which exposed organised crime on high streets, revealing shops selling illegal cigarettes, vapes, cannabis and cocaine, enabling illegal working and suspected money-laundering.

The Conservatives and Reform said the proposals would lead to "more empty" shops, without tax relief for other small businesses.

Burnham said the measures will give councils more power to control what businesses open in town centres.

The proposals come as the prime minister embarks on a tour of the UK, with Downing Street saying he will be in "listening mode" during his visits as he works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

The plans announced by the government include:

Changes to planning law which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open (England only)

Tightening the definition of a vape shop to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer (England only)

Scrapping a rule known as "aim to permit", which currently restricts councils' ability to refuse new betting shops and 24-hour slot machine shops (Great Britain-wide)

Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines (England only)

New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops found to be selling illegal tobacco for up to twelve months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer (England and Wales)

The National Crime Agency (NCA) estimates that at least Â£1bn of criminal cash is laundered through high street stores in the UK each year through businesses connected to the sale of fake goods, tax evasion, illegal working and illegal drug supply.

Burnham told the BBC that the changes would make it "easier for police to close a vape shop and have it closed for longer".

He said: "At the same time we're changing the planning regime... which should stop the proliferation of vape shops on our high streets."

The prime minister added that Operation Vulcan in Cheetham Hill, Greater Manchester, cleared the area of counterfeits and crime and "proved" what could be achieved.

"When I look at police reform across England, I will be asking for a similar approach to be taken," he said. "I want the strongest possible neighbourhood policing, with all agencies involved, to rip out criminal behaviour that is pulling places down."

Burnham said he did not accept the decline of the high street as "inevitable".

"I don't see why anywhere should have to accept they have empty shops, vape shops and the challenges that come with that."

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday that many people were frustrated at vape and gambling outlets "popping up even near schools and some of them are linked to illegal activity and crime".

News.title: Man dies after punch from security guard in Turkey bar, inquest hears
News.content:
A rugby player was punched in the head by a security guard while on holiday in Turkey and died after he returned home, an inquest has heard.

Scot James, from Maesteg, Bridgend county, had been in hospital since he suffered head and brain injuries in an alleged bar assault on 5 July.

He fell and hit his head during a "verbal exchange", Pontypridd Coroner's Court was told on Tuesday.

The 34-year-old was repatriated to the UK and died on 26 July at the Royal Glamorgan Hospital in Llantrisant, Rhondda Cynon Taf.

A provisional cause of death was given as blunt head injury.

James' family described him as a "loving father, son, grandson and partner" in tributes following his death.

Maesteg Celtic RFC said he was an "outstanding player and a great character".

Coroner Rachel Knight said a full inquest was necessary as there was reason to suspect the death may have been unnatural.

She said that as police in Turkey would potentially be investigating James' death, the next inquest hearing would be scheduled for later this year.

Knight said it may be necessary to pause inquest proceedings pending the outcome of any criminal investigation and confirmed the court would liaise with Turkish authorities.

Police in Turkey are understood to be investigating the death, with assistance from the Foreign Office.

In a statement, James' family said he "had a warm heart, a great sense of humour, and a natural ability to bring people together".

"We are heartbroken by his loss," they said.

"No words can truly express the pain we are experiencing or the void his passing has left in our lives."

Maesteg Celtic RFC said: "Everyone at the club is devastated by this news and our thoughts go out to his family and friends at this difficult time."

News.title: England set to be one of the first countries to eliminate hepatitis C
News.content:
Hepatitis C is spread through contact with blood infected with the virus, such as by sharing needles with someone who has it.

Donor blood is already screened for it.

It is a silent disease, meaning people often have no symptoms until much later.

Untreated, it can cause serious and potentially life-threatening liver damage.

NHS England says that since 2015, more than 100,000 people have been diagnosed and treated for hepatitis C, meaning the country is already meeting that target.

Another goal - a 65% reduction in hepatitis C-related mortality compared with 2015 levels - has yet to be met, but might be before the 2030 target date.

Around 50,200 adults are living with hepatitis C, figures for England in 2024 suggest.

Estimates indicate 84.6% of those living with hepatitis C have been diagnosed - just short of the 90% target.

The Hepatitis C Trust says England is "on the cusp" of one of the most significant public health achievements in our country's history.

Prof Frankie Swords, NHS national medical director, added: "England is now leading the world in the mission to eliminate this disease and on course to beat the WHO's 2030 target, but we are determined to keep up the momentum and finish the job.

"We are committed to finding and treating everyone who needs support and would urge those at greater risk to come forward by ordering a free and confidential home-testing kit online."

Adults born in Ukraine, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Albania, Lithuania, Bulgaria, Czechia or Slovakia are particularly urged to test, as some may have been infected through medical or dental procedures before 1991.

People can order a free, confidential NHS home self-testing kit, external without needing to speak to a GP.

Sir Rod Stewart has cancelled the remainder of his 2026 US tour dates after undergoing heart surgery.

The 81-year-old singer, who was performing his One Last Time tour, will take four weeks off to recover after undergoing a coronary stent procedure, effectively cutting short the US and Mexico performances for the remainder of the year, which was due to stretch into September.

He was scheduled to perform events across Ohio, Illinois and Mexico, as well as a six-night stretch at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas.

“I’m already feeling better and very much on the mend,” he said in a post on Instagram.

“I want to thank the doctors, nurses and everyone who has taken such wonderful care of me.

“I am deeply disappointed to miss these shows and sorry to let my fans down, but I look forward to getting back on stage and having a good time with you all again soon.”

His representatives said Sir Rod was “doing very well” following the procedure and had “returned to his normal daily activities”.

The statement added: “On the advice of his doctors, he will take the next four weeks to recuperate and regain full fitness before returning to the stage.

“Unfortunately, this means he will be unable to continue his current tour dates.

“Information regarding affected performances will be communicated by the respective promoters and venues.”

Two further dates in Colorado are scheduled for September 2027.

The announcement came after Sir Rod postponed shows in Cincinnati and Cleveland following medical concerns.

Two further dates in Colorado are scheduled for September 2027 ( Getty )

Cleveland’s Rocket Arena earlier confirmed the cancellation on social media, writing: “Following a period of monitoring, doctors have advised Rod Stewart to rest for at least 48 hours. As a result, his performance tomorrow night, August 11, 2026 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland has been cancelled.

“Rod is disappointed to miss the show and appreciates everyone’s understanding. He looks forward to returning to the stage soon.”

Health problems had also forced the cancellation and postponement of shows in May and June.

In May, the Maggie May singer sent “apologies to my family of fans” in a statement to the Las Vegas Review-Journal after cancelling performances in Nevada, adding: “I am on vocal rest as I recover from a sinus infection.”

Less than a month later, he cancelled his San Diego show after being diagnosed with a respiratory infection that resulted in laryngitis.

Earlier this month, the rocker welcomed his sixth grandchild after his daughter Ruby gave birth to a son called Levi.

Australian prosecutors have dropped two assault-related charges against the man who became a national hero after disarming one of the gunmen during the Bondi Beach shooting last December.

Ahmed al-Ahmed, 44, was charged in June with domestic violence common assault, stalking, and intimidation following an alleged incident involving his father in southwest Sydney in March.

He denied the charges, saying they were “untrue” and that he was “shocked” by the situation.

On Wednesday, prosecutors withdrew the charges at a Sydney court after Mr Ahmed agreed to abide by an apprehended domestic violence order for 12 months, restricting his contact with his father.

“It’s a family situation he never expected, one would never want to expect, and it must be really difficult for him,” his lawyer Mohamad Sakr said in June.

“He is a heroic man and his honesty and dignity should be maintained until these matters are ultimately determined.”

Mr Ahmed said he felt “successful”.

“The law has been served,” he said.

Mr Ahmed declined to comment on his relationship with his father, but said he hoped for “peace”.

“I’m a free man,” he said.

Mr Ahmed became widely known after a video showed him disarming one of the two shooters during the Bondi attack, which was carried out by Sajid Akram and his son Naveed Akram.

While the father was shot dead by police at the scene, the son was arrested and charged with as many as 59 offences, including 15 counts of murder and one of committing a terrorist attack.

Ahmed al Ahmed, centre, gestures during the 'Light Will Win' memorial service, part of the day of mourning for the victims of the Bondi Beach shooting, at the Sydney Opera House on 22 January 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

Mr Ahmed, who was shot multiple times in the arm, was later honoured with the keys to the cities of Canterbury-Bankstown and Waverley.

A fundraiser launched in the days after the shooting collected more than A$2.5m, about £1.24m, for Mr Ahmed, who was visited in hospital by Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese.

In a separate court case, Mr Ahmed had claimed his brothers, Sameh Al Ahmed and Hozifa Al Ahmed, were trying to extort A$200,000 from him. They pleaded not guilty.

“This situation is untrue, it’s extortion,” he told Sydney radio 2GB in June, “and my two brothers have been harassing me, abusing me and pushing to get money from me.”

Mr Sakr said the past few weeks “had been a very stressful experience” for his client and so the Wednesday court order was “a great outcome for all”.

“My client was entitled to the presumption of innocence; that innocence is maintained,” he said.

Astronomers have shared photographs of glasses used to view eclipses almost one hundred years ago, ahead of the best solar eclipse in decades.

More than 90 per cent of the sun will be obscured by the moon between 6.17pm and 8.06pm on Wednesday, the most it has been blocked above UK skies since the total eclipse in 1999.

Convenience stores, national parks and the Royal Greenwich Observatory have all exhausted their glasses supplies ahead of the eclipse, which will be the country’s fullest for the next 54 years.

The Royal Greenwich Observatory alone is said to have sold 15,000 pairs of eclipse glasses in the last month.

On Wednesday, images from the Royal Society showed “Eclipsia” glasses specially designed for viewing eclipses almost a hundred years ago.

The red and black rectangular glasses came with a book of instructions along with an Ordnance Survey map showing the areas of totality in England, the society said.

open image in gallery The Royal Society of the Eclipsia viewing screen ( PA )

The images from the Royal Society were released on Wednesday along with others of photographic glass plates taken of a total solar eclipse in 1875.

The plates have been returned by the society to the Royal Astronomical Society in London after being rediscovered in an archive.

They include images captured by 23-year-old physicist Arthur Schuster, who joined a Royal Society expedition to Thailand, then Siam, to view the eclipse.

open image in gallery Photographic glass plates taken of a total solar eclipse in 1875 ( PA )

Meanwhile, experts have warned that only special solar eclipse glasses that are ISO 12312-2 certified for the safest eye protection should be used to view Wednesday’s eclipse and that sunglasses were not sufficient.

Following the 1999 total solar eclipse, the Royal College of Ophthalmologists reported around 70 cases of people experiencing vision problems after watching the eclipse, with around 40 per cent having looked at it for less than a minute.

Mohamed Elalfy, a consultant ophthalmologist and president of the Royal College of Ophthalmologists, said: “The safest way to enjoy the eclipse is to observe it indirectly, such as by watching a live broadcast.

“Looking directly at the sun during a solar eclipse can cause damage to the retina, potentially damaging the cells responsible for sharp central vision.

“Crucially, the retina has no pain receptors, so people will not feel the damage as it happens.

“Symptoms may only become apparent several hours later and can include blurred vision, a central blind or dark spot, distorted vision, reduced colour perception and increased sensitivity to light.

“While some people recover over weeks or months, others can be left with permanent visual impairment.”

Demi Lovato’s role in Camp Rock 3 has been confirmed after months of fan speculation.

The singer, 33, starred in the first two hit Disney Channel original movies in 2008 and 2010 alongside the Jonas Brothers, who were previously confirmed to be starring in the new film as well as serving as executive producers.

Lovato was also initially named as an executive producer without an on-screen role, but film execs stayed quiet and kept fans pleading for answers about whether she would appear in the third film — until now.

Disney producers announced Monday that Lovato will reprise her role as Mitchie Torres for a brief cameo in the new movie, which debuts Thursday.

The “Skyscraper” singer, who skyrocketed to fame after the release of the original Camp Rock movie, reunited with Joe, Kevin and Nick Jonas at Monday’s Los Angeles premiere. She went on to share throwback pictures from the first two movies on Instagram, writing, “mitchie 4 ever #thisisme.”

open image in gallery Kevin Jonas, Nick Jonas, Demi Lovato and Joe Jonas attended the world premiere for 'Camp Rock 3' ( Reuters )

Fans have been theorizing about Lovato’s part in the new movie after she surprised the crowd at the opening night of the Jonas Brothers’s tour at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey last August to perform “This is Me” from the 2008 film and “Wouldn’t Change a Thing” from the 2010 sequel.

“What do you mean you won't be in Camp Rock 3? You're the star; it doesn't make sense for you not to be there,” one user wrote to Lovato on Instagram. Another shared in the comments, “ima need you in the movie!!!!! Please, that’s the only way I’ll watch. You are what makes the movie! Without you there is no movie.”

Camp Rock and Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam are set at a music camp where Lovato’s character, a shy singer-songwriter, attends while her mom, played by Maria Canals-Barrera, works as the camp’s cook. Canals-Barrera will also be reprising her role in the new film.

In the movies, Mitchie sparks a romance with boy band member Shane Gray, played by Joe Jonas. The Jonas Brothers star as Connect 3, a fictionalized version of their real-life band of brothers.

open image in gallery Demi Lovato will reprise her role as Mitchie Torres in a brief cameo in the film ( Disney )

Camp Rock 3 will follow Connect 3’s return to Camp Rock to find an opening act for their reunion tour. The newcomers include Liamani Segura, who stars as the “bold and determined” Sage opposite the “camp bad boy” Fletch played by Malachi Burton, according to the movie’s official logline.

The cast also includes Lumi Pollack, Sherry Cola, Hudson Stone, Casey Trotter, Brooklynn Pitts and Ava Jean.

Veronica Rodriguez, who directed the new movie from a screenplay by Eydie Faye, told The Hollywood Reporter in an interview published Monday that she wanted to strike “the right balance” with Lovato’s involvement in the film.

“Her character literally says in the movie, to her mom, ‘This isn’t about me, it’s about them. It’s their time to shine. This is the new generation of campers,’” Rodriguez explained. “With Mitchie and Connect 3, we wanted them to be ingrained and necessary for the story but also leave enough room and space for the world to fall in love with the new generation of campers.”

Rosario Dawson has spoken out about her filmed cameo in Spider-Man: Brand New Day that didn’t make the final cut.

The Star Wars: Ahsoka actor, 47, was originally expected to appear in the latest Marvel blockbuster as her Daredevil character Claire Temple/Night Nurse. But her scene was ultimately “cut out,” she revealed last month at GalaxyCon Raleigh 2026.

“I told my mom, and she was like, ‘That sucks. Now I can’t post the pictures,’ and I was like, ‘Right, mom, me being cut out of the movie that has like the largest viewership of a trailer ever, the issue is you can’t post your BTS photos,’” Dawson joked, according to The Wrap.

“When I tell you my post was already ready with my BTS, with like my grandson wearing all his Spider-Man stuff because he loves Spider-Man — then I got the email done,” she explained. “So yeah. I’m a reject of Spider-Man.”

Dawson starred as Claire Temple, a crucial medical ally and romantic interest to Charlie Cox’s superhero Matt Murdoch/Daredevil, in the three-season superhero drama Daredevil, which aired from 2015 to 2018. Daredevil and Spider-Man famously exist in the same live-action universe, with Cox even making a cameo in Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021).

open image in gallery Zendaya and Tom Holland reprise their roles as MJ and Peter Parker in ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ ( Sony )

open image in gallery Rosario Dawson filmed a cameo scene for 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' that ultimately got cut due to time constraints ( Getty )

“I would love — I still, because everybody’s in it, it still means that my character is somewhere in that same universe, and I really love that,” Dawson said. “So I hope I get to be Claire again.”

The deleted Brand New Day scene showed Claire helping Tom Holland’s Peter Parker/Spider-Man into the hospital after his fight against Scorpion (Michael Mando), according to The Wrap.

Screenwriters Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers previously confirmed to the outlet that Dawson’s scene was likely removed due to runtime constraints.

“Rosario Dawson is great. I wasn’t there for those discussions. But it was great. If anything, you have a movie that is two-and-a-half hours long, and it’s almost an embarrassment of riches with so many great characters and so many great scenes,” McKenna said.

open image in gallery ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ is out now in theaters ( Sony Pictures )

“The scene they did was a good scene; I think the only reason it’s not in the final cut was just it was probably cut for time because it was very good,” Sommers added.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day marks Holland’s fourth solo outing as the web-slinging superhero, alongside Zendaya. The new film, which also stars Sadie Sink, Jon Bernthal and Jacob Batalon, is both a critical and massive box-office success, having earned $1.6 million globally in its second week.

“This is the best Spider-Man movie in more than 20 years,” The Independent’s Clarisse Loughrey boldly proclaimed in a four-star review.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register or login to an existing telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football launched on August 10, 2026. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.

How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.
