News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games. Last season Mark Flekken came out on top with 153 saves for Brentford, so it will be interesting to see how Caoimhin Kelleher gets on this season.



What counts as a Save?



A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

For an exhaustive list of how to score Telegraph Fantasy Football points, take a look at our Game Guidelines.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

Sports.title: Paul Pogba, 33, ‘set to have Monaco contract terminated’ after injury-hit return to football following doping ban
Sports.content:
MONACO are reportedly in talks to terminate Paul Pogba’s contract.

The former Manchester United midfielder, 33, was given the chance to resurrect his career in the Principality last summer after serving a doping ban.



But he has played just 115 minutes of football across six appearances.

And now, according to The Athletic, Pogba and Monaco are thrashing out the terms of a deal that will see them part ways immediately.



Pogba still has a year left to run on his Monaco deal but if the termination goes through he will be free to seek his next club as a free agent.

The 2018 World Cup winner has struggled with fitness and injuries since returning to the professional game last year.



And he suffered a hamstring problem during Monaco’s pre-season tour of England that could now sideline him for several MONTHS.

That is not thought to be the driving force behind the separation talks, however, as negotiations are said to have been rumbling on for several weeks.

Pogba broke down in tears when signing his two-year Monaco deal in 2025.

There was over two years between his final appearance for Juventus and his debut for Monaco, having served part of a four-year doping ban which was reduced to 18 months on appeal by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Pogba joined United’s academy from Le Havre in 2009 and made seven first-team appearances before joining Juve on a free.

The Frenchman was an instant hit in Italy and re-signed for United in a whopping £89million deal four years later – a world record at the time.

Pogba netted 39 goals in 226 games during an up-and-down second stint with the Red Devils.



He has only played 18 professional matches since leaving Old Trafford in 2022.

Sports.title: Chelsea Files: How The Avengers convinced club legend to join Blues, Xabi Alonso set to cull 40-man squad
Sports.content:
DID you know that The Avengers had a part to play in one of Chelsea’s greatest ever players joining them in 1996?

Apart from it wasn’t Spider-Man, The Hulk and Iron Man convincing Gianluca Vialli to leave Juventus for Stamford Bridge, it was a 1960s TV show with the same name.



Vialli’s move to Chelsea at the time seemed to make no sense.

Juventus had just won the Champions League, with the Blues having just placed 11th in the Premier League, ironically not too dissimilar to where they were last season before spending a bucket-load on Morgan Rogers this summer.



Asked about the move, one of Vialli’s lifelong friends, Luca Dal Monte, exclusively told SunSport about his decision to come to Stamford Bridge.

Dal Monte said: “Gianluca’s decision to join Chelsea was not just a football decision. If you look at it purely in football terms, it made very little sense.



“He was leaving Juventus, who had just won the Champions League, for a Chelsea side that had finished 11th in the Premier League.

“I remember that a few years earlier, when Silvio Berlusconi was making his second attempt to take him to AC Milan, I had actually argued with Gianluca about the importance of winning trophies.

“I remember telling him that a great player becomes truly great not only because of the way he plays or the goals he scores, but also because of the silverware he wins.

“Leaving the Champions of Europe immediately after winning the Champions League seemed almost incomprehensible. But Gianluca felt that his time in Italy had come to an end.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“He had won almost everything there was to win, first with Sampdoria and then with Juventus, and at 32 he wanted something different, not simply another club but another experience of life.

“London had a particular fascination for Italians of our generation. For many of us, it was the destination of our first flight, often for an Easter holiday when we were teenagers.

“Britain had also entered our imagination through television. We had grown up under the spell of British series such as The Avengers – “Mrs Peel, we’re needed!” – and London seemed exciting, stylish and somehow different from anywhere else.

“I think there was also something very characteristic of Gianluca in the decision. He was curious. He was never frightened by change. He could have remained in Italy, where he was famous, successful and completely at home.



“But instead, he chose to put himself in a country where he barely spoke the language and where the football culture was entirely different. In a sense, he chose uncertainty. What he could not possibly have known was how profoundly that decision would change his life.

“Chelsea was supposed to be the next chapter of his career. Instead, it became part of his identity. He arrived as a famous Italian footballer and became a Chelsea man, and Stamford Bridge really did capture his heart.”

Vialli, who arned 59 caps for Italy, tragically died in 2023 at the age of 58 following a six-year battle with cancer.

More of Dal Monte’s tales of his treasured relationship with Vialli can be found in his new biography: The Gentleman: Gianluca Vialli and How He Changed English Football Forever.

MAHD WORLD

MAHDI NICOLL-JAZULI and Reggie Watson looked like the future of Chelsea during the pre-season tour.



But the challenge now is to turn future into present, for them and the rest of the Blues’ impressive crop of youngsters.

MNJ and Watson are still only 16. So although they proved they could mix it in men’s football in Australia and the Far East, and sometimes showed up their more experienced team-mates, loan moves away from Cobham feel unlikely.

The pair’s development may well be best served by “playing up” in PL2 and the Premier League International Cup, competitions for Under-21s, as well as in the Under-18s.

Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, Reggie Walsh and Shim Mheuka are on a different path.

All three have already had a taste of first-team football. Mheuka was also the top goalscorer and player of the season in PL2 last year and surely needs a loan to at least a Championship club, or a top-flight side abroad, in order to take the next step.



Winger Kavuma-McQueen, 17, is being strongly linked with a loan move to Portsmouth. He looks to have the confidence as well as the ability to make an impression in the second tier.

Walsh, also 17 but with a much-improved physique, is now more likely to be able to impose his creative skills, and a spell at League One Wigan is in the offing.

Jesse Derry, who made an eventful first-team debut at the end of the last campaign, has already gone to Sporting Lisbon for the season.

Chelsea have no first-team European football this campaign so much of the hard work for the remainder of the window will involve cutting Xabi Alonso’s squad of around 40 to a more manageable number.

But the club will also be busy finalising plans to make sure the best prospects of the Academy, who also include 17-year-old “Moroccan Messi” Ibrahim Rabbaj, have the best chance of becoming first-team players as soon as possible.



STRAS RELIEF

STRASBOURG fans will doubtless continue their protests against the BlueCo owners they share with Chelsea.

As things stand, Alonso’s first-team squad will contain the former spine of their sister club’s team.

Mike Penders, Mamadou Sarr, Valentin Barco and Emmanuel Emegha are all now in England.



However they perform, Strasbourg fans will feel sore and even more justified in believing their interests and aspirations are being sacrificed for Chelsea’s benefit.

If the quartet are given a chance by Alonso and do well, it will reaffirm the Ligue 1 team’s status as a glorified feeder club.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If one or more of them barely play for the Blues or are sold or sent out on loan elsewhere, the fans will legitimately question why they were not left in Strasbourg.

Players moving the other way across the English Channel, with goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen set to replace Penders, will do little to appease supporters no matter how well the team does on the pitch.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola agreed to feature in Jose Mourinho’s Netflix doc but backed out after his one condition was not met
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO’S biggest rivals are conspicuous by their absence from his new Netflix documentary.

The three-part series about the former Chelsea and Real Madrid boss has already got football fans talking, with Mourinho revealing a number of fascinating stories from his remarkable career.



One of the biggest revelations is that Mourinho was lined up to replace Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager before ultimately deciding against it and returning to Chelsea.

The documentary features a host of Mourinho favourites, including John Terry and Frank Lampard as well as the man he was once expected to succeed, Ferguson.



There is even a surprise appearance from Iker Casillas, despite the former Real Madrid goalkeeper being strongly against Mourinho returning to the Spanish giants this summer.

Casillas lost his place as Real Madrid’s No.1 during Mourinho’s reign, with the Portuguese coach hinting that the goalkeeper was leaking dressing-room information to the media.

Their relationship deteriorated, with Casillas’ close friendships with Barcelona players such as Gerard Pique becoming another source of tension.

The fierce rivalry between Real Madrid and Barcelona only added to the drama.

But despite their history, Casillas features in the documentary and is given the chance to tell his side of the story.

So why are some of Mourinho’s biggest rivals missing?

Pep Guardiola



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Perhaps the most surprising omission is Pep Guardiola.

The pair famously developed one of football’s fiercest managerial rivalries during their time in charge of Barcelona and Real Madrid.

But their relationship goes back much further, with Guardiola and Mourinho having worked together at Barcelona.

They later found themselves on opposite sides of Manchester, with Mourinho managing United and Guardiola in charge of City.



Given their history, Guardiola would have been an obvious choice for the documentary.

And SunSport has been told that he was approached.

Guardiola was reportedly open to taking part and sharing his experiences of going head-to-head with Mourinho.

But there was one major condition.

Director Joe Pearlman – the multi-Emmy, Bafta, and Grammy-nominated British documentary maker – told The Sun: “Yes, we did reach out to Pep, who agreed to do an interview but it was on the condition that Jose reached out to him in person.



“You can imagine how that went down.”

Roman Abramovich

Another major absentee is former Chelsea owner Roman Abramovich.



Mourinho first came to widespread English attention when he famously celebrated by running down the Old Trafford touchline after Porto knocked Manchester United out of the Champions League.

That performance is widely regarded as one of the moments that convinced Abramovich he wanted the feisty Portuguese at Chelsea.

Mourinho would go on to become one of the most successful managers in the club’s history, winning two Premier League titles during his first spell at Stamford Bridge.

Yet Abramovich does not feature in the documentary.

SunSport asked Pearlman why they did not pursue an interview with the former Chelsea owner.



He said: “Mr Abramovich has a lot of interviews he should probably do before he talks about his tenure at Chelsea, so no, it wasn’t something we pursued, especially as Peter Kenyon gives the exact same account.”

Arsene Wenger

Then there is Arsene Wenger.



The Frenchman and Mourinho had one of the most entertaining managerial feuds in Premier League history.

Their rivalry produced plenty of memorable moments, with Mourinho famously branding Wenger a “specialist in failure”.

So why was Wenger not interviewed?

Pearlman admits the documentary makers simply did not pursue him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “Wenger says it all in the press conferences, but the honest truth is that we just did not bother reaching out to him.”



While Mourinho’s career has provided plenty of drama, it seems some of the biggest names from his story were either unwilling or simply not approached for the final cut.

Sports.title: Man Utd have made six signings, let 14 players leave and could still secure seven transfers
Sports.content:
Man Utd have made six signings, let 14 players leave and could still secure seven transfers

Manchester United have continued their high level of activity in the summer transfer window

View 9 Images Michael Carrick is making moves in the transfer window (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has been busy building his Manchester United squad for the upcoming 2026/27 season, with a number of transfers heading in and out of Old Trafford. The new club confirmed his permanent stay as manager towards the end of last season, following a successful stint in temporary charge since January.

‌



A number of stars have returned for pre-season training already, including out-of-favour winger Marcus Rashford. The 28-year-old is said to be "excited" to work under the ex-United captain next season, with The Athletic reporting that the academy graduate is looking forward to the upcoming campaign.

‌



The likes of Casemiro and Jadon Sancho have exited the building in Manchester following the expiry of their contracts, with 12 more also no longer at Old Trafford. But with the Premier League season beginning on August 22 against Hull City, Carrick will be keen to bring more stars in quickly.

‌



Here, Mirror Football has detailed the current state of play at Old Trafford right now.

Who have Man Utd signed so far?

Andrey Santos was the first signing of the Carrick era, joining from Chelsea for a £50 million fee. The midfielder has been a constant presence in United's pre-season fixtures and is confident he can replace Casemiro as the No. 6 this season.

‌



Speaking after the 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain, Santos said: "I prefer playing deep like a number six. I try help my teammates without the ball and with the ball I love breaking the lines. For me Casemiro is a legend. Now he's gone and I'm here. I feel that I can do like Casemiro did last season."

View 9 Images Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have joined United this summer (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Goalkeeper Karl Darlow was next to join the squad, leaving Leeds on a free transfer and heading to Old Trafford. Aston Villa's Youri Tielemans was the second midfielder to hop on the Carrick train, with United exercising the £35m release clause to sign the 29-year-old.

‌



Youth signings Tynan Thompson and Kit Margetson also joined from Tottenham and Swansea City, respectively. United most recently secured Cristian Orozco from Fortaleza CEIF, with the 18-year-old midfielder joining the United academy to gain experience in England.

Who has left Man Utd?

View 9 Images Sancho and Casemiro's salaries are now off the wage bill (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

A whopping 14 players have left United this summer, including a few big names on the wage bill. Casemiro joined Inter Miami on a free transfer, taking £350,000 off the weekly salary output.

‌



Jadon Sancho, Tyrell Malacia and Malachi Sharpe have all left upon the expiry of their contracts and are without a club for the time being. Radek Vitek recently joined Middlesbrough, with reports claiming that an initial fee of £7m had been agreed, which could double if performance bonuses are met.

In terms of loans, Solomon Honor has moved to Southport, Sekou Kone has arrived at Lausanne-Sport and Andre Onana returned to Trabzonspor for a second temporary spell. Altay Bayindir joined Celta Vigo on loan earlier this week and Elyh Harrison headed north to spend the season at Greenock Morton.

Sonny Aljofree has moved to Rotherham United on a free transfer, with James Bailey heading to Stockport County in a similar deal. Tyler Fredricson has ended his eight-year association with United by joining Lausanne-Sport on a permanent deal in Switzerland.

‌



View 9 Images Rasmus Hojlund has left Manchester for Napoli (Image: Ciro De Luca/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Finally, Rasmus Hojlund joined Napoli following a successful loan in Italy. The Serie A side had a £38m obligation-to-buy clause, provided they qualified for the Champions League.

This was achieved after they finished second in the 2025/26 campaign, and Hojlund confirmed his move by scoring against Pisa to secure the European spot. Writing on Instagram in May, the Denmark international said: "This goal felt symbolic because it means two things. We now secured Champions League with Napoli, which means because of my contract I’m now officially a Napoli player and I’m saying goodbye to Manchester United.

‌



"My childhood dream came true by playing at Old Trafford in a red jersey. So the goal today symbolises a new confident start, in which I will give everything for the time ahead to Napoli, and a thank you to all the fans, players and staff of Manchester United who made the dream I had as a kid come true. It’s time for new dreams, so let’s chase them."

Seven transfers that can still be done

View 9 Images United are keen to bring Louis Page to Old Trafford (Image: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

‌



More transfers could still be achieved at United, with potentially three more incoming and four heading out the exit door. The Red Devils are currently working on a deal to bring Louis Page to the club.

The Leicester City midfielder has become an impressive talent despite his club's relegation to League One. The 18-year-old was named EFL Apprentice of the Year and has already made 21 senior appearances so far.

BBC Sport reports that talks are ongoing, with Aston Villa and Arsenal also interested, but United are the frontrunners in the transfer conversation. The club are also looking at fullbacks to bolster their defensive department with Jorge Salinas emerging as a target.

‌



Previous reports have claimed that the left-back is regarded as a huge talent and could provide United with a long-term plan to replace Luke Shaw. Racing Santander sporting director Chema Aragon has made it clear that clubs will have to reach their £13.7m release clause if they plan to sign the defender, adding: "There is nothing we can do if a big star appears."

9 View 9 Images Jorge Salinas has been linked (Image: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) 9 View 9 Images Lewis Hall is still a huge target for Carrick (Image: Ed Sykes/Getty Images)

‌



Lewis Hall remains the primary target for United, but Newcastle are adamant the 21-year-old is not for sale. The transfers of Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Bruno Guimaraes have prompted the Magpies to close ranks and try to keep their remaining key stars at St James' Park this summer.

Myles Lewis-Skelly could be one alternative who can provide proven Premier League experience in place of Hall, with United being offered the opportunity to sign the 19-year-old this week. Following the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, the Gunners have opened up to the prospect of selling the young star this summer.

Lewis-Skelly can operate as a full-back as well as a midfielder and could be a versatile addition to Carrick's squad. One more midfielder is expected to arrive, with Manu Kone also having been strongly linked with a move to Old Trafford during this window.

‌



Reports suggest that the Roma star has emerged as a midfield target, and Corriere dello Sport claims that personal terms have been agreed. However, the Serie A side will reportedly demand up to £51m (€60m) for his services.

‌



Lamine Camara has also been linked with United as a possible alternative, with The Standard reporting that he will cost at least £42.7m (€50m). With Page looking likely to be an academy addition, another midfielder and a left-back could wrap up United's summer incoming business.

But with this amount potentially coming in, Carrick will look to offload some stars this summer. Toby Collyer has interest from a number of Championship sides with The Athletic reporting that a loan or permanent move is possible.

Harry Amass is also a subject of transfer interest despite featuring heavily during United's pre-season tour of Europe. It is reported that the club are open to a transfer if the left-back's £6m fee is met, but a loan could also be on the cards.

Article continues below

Joshua Zirkzee has been continuously connected to Juventus in recent months. The Serie A side are considering a loan with obligation to buy, as per The Athletic, with other clubs said to be interested in the striker. Ethan Wheatley is being monitored by Everton currently to bolster their under-21 set-up.

“We are looking at several different parameters. First and foremost, it is about Ifeanyi getting a lot of playing time,and then Liverpool is also looking at what type of football clubs play, as they want him to play in a high-pressing defence, so it is a bit like what you see in Liverpool.

“Since Ifeanyi has just joined Liverpool, it is of course a loan deal without an option to buy. But for now I can’t say much more.”

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Myles Lewis-Skelly transfer bombshell as club puts three players up for sale

Manchester United could be faced with a rare transfer opportunity following a surprise development regarding Arsenal youngster Myles Lewis-Skelly

View 3 Images Michael Carrick's first pre-season as Manchester United manager is almost in the books (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick's first summer transfer window in charge of Manchester United continues to look very promising as the new season moves within sight. His side have already added personnel in key areas but continue to be linked with a host of names.

‌



This summer, United are undefeated in three pre-season outings since suffering defeat to Wrexham in their friendly opener. Carrick & Co drew 1-1 against European champions Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday as Bryan Mbeumo netted his third goal in two games.

‌



However, the Premier League giants are looking to keep levelling up after already adding Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans to their midfield. And Arsenal could provide some timely transfer aid as Mirror Football rounds up the latest rumours coming out of Old Trafford.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea and Man Utd offered Myles Lewis-Skelly as Arsenal open to shock sale despite new deal READ MORE :

Audacious Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed with Arsenal star joining Man Utd READ MORE :

Lewis-Skelly offered to United

The £75million addition of Bruno Guimaraes looks set to have a domino effect at the Emirates Stadium. That's following reports that Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to both United and Chelsea this week.

View 3 Images Lewis-Skelly may seek an Arsenal exit (Image: Getty)

‌



Despite showing great promise as a left-back prospect initially, Mikel Arteta utilised Lewis-Skelly in midfield last term. The 19-year-old made some crucial contributions towards the end of last season as the Gunners clinched the Premier League and made it to the Champions League final.

It just so happens United have a serious need for a new left-back as they search for a long-term successor to Luke Shaw. Newcastle's Lewis Hall has been strongly linked as a candidate for that role, though the Magpies reportedly aren't willing to sell.

‌



football.london reported the Lewis-Skelly proposal first, with Arteta seemingly settled on Jurrien Timber, Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie as his left-back options. Chelsea could be a major threat to any plans to sign Lewis-Skelly, too, given he's from London and previously trained at Cobham as a youth.

The teenager would fit United's transfer needs, considering they're understood to be chasing one more midfield option, along with a new left-back prospect. The England international ticks both boxes, though it remains to be seen exactly how much Arsenal want for Lewis-Skelly's signature.

Real trio up for sale

Elsewhere, Jose Mourinho is reportedly open to selling off three names deemed surplus to requirements at Real Madrid. And United could be in the running to capitalise on one or more of those available assets.

‌



View 3 Images Camavinga could leave Real Madrid (Image: Getty)

According to Spanish publication AS, 'The Special One' has said he wants a squad of 20, plus the currently injured trio of Rodrygo, Eder Militao and Ferland Mendy. However, Mendy is one of those players who could be moved on due to the level of competition at left-back now that Marc Cucurella has arrived.

Mendy has no intention of leaving the Bernabeu, but his injury record has failed to inspire belief in Madrid. Ex-United prospect Alvaro Carreras is the other left-back option believed to be ahead of the Frenchman in the pecking order. If Mendy does change his tune, this could turn United heads.

‌



Eduardo Camavinga is in a similar position and does not want to leave Real. United have been strongly linked with the midfielder in the past and could make use of his talents, given Camavinga has previously proved himself competent in midfield or at left-back.

The other Real name supposedly up for grabs is academy graduate Raul Asencio. However, United aren't currently thought to be actively searching for new faces in central defence.

United have already experienced consistent frustration with Shaw's unavailability due to injuries over the years. For that reason, Camavinga may not be the only name reportedly available for transfer at Real with a genuine chance of joining United this summer.

And now, a supercomputer simulated by Casino Kings has Nuno Espirito Santo's side topping the table ahead of their first game of the season at Burnley on Sunday.

Sports.title: Real Madrid plot shock Martin Zubimendi transfer as Arsenal left with dilemma
Sports.content:
Real Madrid plot shock Martin Zubimendi transfer as Arsenal left with dilemma

Real Madrid failed with a late attempt to lure Martin Zubimendi to the Bernabeu last summer but could now make another play for the Spaniard's services this month

View 2 Images Martin Zubimendi is again being courted by Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Real Madrid are said to be considering a surprise swoop for Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi - 12 months after failing to hijack the midfield maestro's move to the Premier League champions.

‌



Zubimendi was courted by a whole host of Europe's elite during his time at Real Sociedad with Liverpool going close to signing the 27-year-old back in the summer of 2024. The player had a late change of heart back then and chose to stay in Spain before moving to Arsenal during last summer's transfer window, despite late interest from Real Madrid.

‌



The playmaker featured in all 38 Premier League matches in his maiden season as a Gunner to help the club win their first league title in more than 20 years.

‌



But with Arsenal splashing out £75million on Bruno Guimaraes to further strengthen their midfield options, The Sun claim Real are ready to rekindle their interest in Zubimendi.

Myles Lewis-Skelly has made his preference clear as Man Utd and Chelsea sounded out READ MORE :

Whether Zubimendi is attainable or not is another matter with Mikel Arteta known to be a huge fan of the midfielder. It is thought, though, that Arsenal will have to sell if they are to give themselves the financial flexibility in the transfer market to 'level up' the team that almost completed the double last year after reaching the Champions League final, as per Arteta's wishes. And that could leave them with some difficult decisions to make in terms of outgoings.

It emerged on Tuesday that another highly-regarded player, Myles Lewis-Skelly, has been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United. It is currently unclear if Arsenal's London rivals will make a move for the 19-year-old Hale End graduate, though United are not expected to.

‌



Real Madrid's need for a midfielder is nothing new and they were previously believed to be the frontrunners to sign Rodri, with the Manchester City star open to a return to Spain this summer.

View 2 Images Real Madrid were favourites to sign Rodri but he now seems to be Barcelona-bound

The 30-year-old has entered the final year of his contract at The Etihad and the former Ballon d'Or winner was viewed as the ideal fit for the midfielder Jose Mourinho wants this summer.

Article continues below

But Real are now said to be behind Barcelona in the race for Rodri's services, even though their arch-rivals have seen an opening bid for the player turned down by City.

Sports.title: Liverpool get 'multiple calls' over taking star who Andoni Iraola is banned from playing
Sports.content:
Liverpool get 'multiple calls' over taking star who Andoni Iraola is banned from playing

The Liverpool young centre-back has enjoyed an impressive Liverpool pre-season so far before leaving out on loan for the new season

View 2 Images Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe is not short of suitors (Image: (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images))

Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe is not short of suitors and he reportedly already favour a move to Portugal. The 18‑year‑old, who joined from Austria Vienna in a £2.5million deal, is expected to be loaned out for the upcoming season.

‌



Ndukwe impressed for the first team during pre‑season friendlies, but must now head out on loan due to work‑permit complications. Liverpool require a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE) from the FA to secure a work visa from the Home Office, yet the defender does not currently qualify, with players needing 15 points across several criteria.

‌



Having made just one senior appearance for Austria Vienna last season and being signed largely on the back of his standout performances at the Under‑17 World Cup in Qatar, he has not yet accumulated enough points to meet the senior international threshold.

‌



Liverpool sign Ronald Araujo as club legend reaches out and Andoni Iraola gets his wish READ MORE :

At the time, his agent Georg Lederer confirmed the plan had changed after the defender failed to qualify for a visa.

"The fact is that in the 2025/26 Premier League season, clubs had two exception spots where they didn't have to reach this points target," he explained to ORF, as quoted by Sky Sports Austria. "In the new season, this extra rule will be reduced by one spot. A loan club will now be found where Ifeanyi can gain playing experience at a very high level."

According to The Mail, clubs in Portugal, Germany, Spain, Denmark and France have all enquired about taking Ndukwe on loan, but there is a growing sense that Portugal may be his preferred destination.

‌



"I can't say which clubs we are in dialogue with, but I can confirm that we are in dialogue with Danish clubs about Ifeanyi Ndukwe," Lederer added. "The only thing I can say is that we are not talking about the top clubs in Denmark.

View 2 Images Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe in action during pre-season (Image: (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images))

"We are also talking to several foreign clubs, but right now we need to decide, in collaboration with Liverpool, where Ifeanyi will fit best. We are looking at several different parameters. First and foremost, it is about Ifeanyi getting a lot of playing time, and then Liverpool are also looking at what type of football clubs play, as they want him in a high-pressing defence, so it is a bit like what you see in Liverpool.

‌



"Since Ifeanyi has just arrived at Liverpool, it is of course a loan agreement without an option to buy, but for now I can't say much more."

Liverpool paid around £2.6m for the teenager in January ahead of his planned move this summer, following his 18th birthday in March. Since then, he has caught the eye in defence during pre‑season outings against Sunderland, Wrexham, Leeds United and Monaco.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Virgil van Dijk, who partnered a player 17 years younger than him in Sunday's 3-2 defeat to Monaco, was left impressed by the youngster.

"Obviously I saw the games in pre-season in America," Van Dijk said. "He's a big talent, big guy and he wants to learn and I had a brief conversation with him, especially in the last couple of days. For him it is just progressing.

"I know he has to go on loan I think so let’s see where he ends up. Yeah [it's a shame he has to move on loan].

Article continues below

"I don’t know exactly what the rules are but the matter of fact is that he has to go on loan and wherever he goes, he needs to learn, get better and be ready when he comes back to hopefully stay there."

Sports.title: Martin Zubimendi dilemma shows Mikel Arteta and Arsenal face new transfer problem
Sports.content:
Martin Zubimendi dilemma shows Mikel Arteta and Arsenal face new transfer problem

Martin Zubimendi is being linked with the Arsenal exit door after only one year and the signing of Bruno Guimaraes suggests the Spaniard will be shunted down the pecking order

View 4 Images Arsenal signing of Bruno Guimaraes could have a knock on affect on the squad (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

When someone of Bruno Guimaraes' calibre arrives at Arsenal, amid all the fanfare, there will be someone wondering if their time is up.

‌



The Brazilian has just moved to the Emirates for £75million after making it known that the Gunners were the club for him. This is a player who could play for any team in Europe and he will inevitably make Arsenal better.

‌



But following his arrival, that leaves one player having to go out and as part of the fallout reports have emerged that Arsenal have named their price on Martin Zubimendi. That generally only happens for players who could be on the move.

‌



You don't see any prices being quoted for Declan Rice, because he's one of Arsenal's untouchables, if they ever did make such a list. Zubimendi less so and after only a year at Arsenal the Spaniard could be set for a new role, and one he may not enjoy, if he stays.

It's a huge change for a player who, it was well documented, Mikel Arteta had eyed for several years before eventually luring him to London. This was a player who dominated England in the Euro 2024 final, making replacing Rodri look a simple task.

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

But elite clubs only go looking for players in areas where they think they can improve. You hear no noise around Arsenal landing a top class centre-half, because in William Saliba and Gabriel, they have what they need. You hear no noise around Manchester City signing a top tier No.9, because they have Erling Haaland.

‌



Arsenal's pursuit of Guimaraes showed that they feel they can upgrade in that position. Rice is their talisman but alongside him there's been plenty of contenders. Mikel Merino is one, albeit very versatile, Zubimendi another. Myles Lewis-Skelly may have ambitions to play in that role.

If Zubimendi is to shift from a player who was guaranteed to start to one who isn't, then perhaps the warning signs were there. This is a player who started 34 of 38 games last season - but was benched for three of the final four.

View 4 Images Martin Zubimendi increasingly found himself on the bench towards the end of the season

‌



The Spaniard's minutes were cut and he endured the embarrassment of being subbed on, and then off, by Arteta. That came in the vital win over West Ham with Zubimendi coming on in the 28th minute for the injured Ben White. But his afternoon lasted less than 40 minutes and he was hauled off in the 67th minute for Kai Havertz.

"It is never easy to do that to a player, especially someone with Martin’s quality," Arteta admitted after the game.

Weeks later and Lewis-Skelly, who had been snubbed for much of the season, was picked to play in the Champions League final against PSG. Zubimendi started on the bench, and that's where he would remain for the evening.

‌



Managers can talk all they want about the value and the importance of a player, but what really tells is whether they call upon them come crunch time. With the title in the balance and a European Cup on the line, Zubimendi found himself overlooked.

View 4 Images The Spaniard did claim the Premier League title in his first campaign with Arsenal

When Zubimendi signed from Real Sociedad the club's sporting director, Andrea Berta, claimed: "Martin was a key target for us and we all know that he is a perfect fit for our squad with the high quality he has."

‌



That fit does not look so perfect now following Arsenal's pursuit of Guimaraes. Arteta has a squad that is the envy of most of Europe, but he'll find that having so many options creates as many problems as solutions it solves.

Arsenal have effectively played with two holding midfielders and a 10, previously Martin Odegaard. The Norwegian too is a man under pressure for his spot. Going on the fact that Rice is the pillar and Guimaraes, the second most expensive player in Arsenal history, will start - where does that leave Zubimendi?

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta has some difficult decisions regarding the make-up of his midfield

‌



A possibility exists that Arsenal play with more of a flat three in midfield. But where does that leave Odegaard. Or Eberechi Eze, who played centrally last season, or Kai Havertz or eventually Max Dowman?

Arsenal were pipped on penalties by PSG last season as their European Cup dreams were ended in heartbreaking fashion. On that night in Budapest, for all their battling spirit and defensive quality, it was clear that the Gunners had levels to go in the final third to match PSG.

This summer has been about closing that gap. Guimaraes is the type of player who helps them play through the lines. Their pursuit of Vinicius Junior was well publicised.

‌



Arsenal are firmly back among Europe's elite, capping an impressive rise under Arteta's leadership, but if there's one conundrum they're yet to face during the assembly of their stunning squad, it is who to back. In recent years no major player has wanted out, but with so many top class operators now available some will inevitably end up being cannon fodder in the club's grand plan.

Zubimendi may be one of the early lessons.

Sports.title: Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow
Sports.content:
Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow

Manchester United are ready to move for Club Brugge left-back Joaquin Seys after seeing their advances for two other targets, including Lewis Hall, knocked back

View 2 Images Joaquin Seys has impressed for Club Brugge with Man Utd now keen

Manchester United are ready to open talks with Club Brugge about a £30million deal for left-back Joaquin Seys after being knocked back by two of their targets.

‌



The Red Devils have added two new faces in midfield but left-back is another area where they are looking to bring in reinforcements. It has proved challenging throughout the summer however with the club onto their third different target.

‌



The Belgian side are in no hurry to sell and have Seys under contract for another three years. They will not ease off their £30m price tag, but it Mirror Football understands United are strongly considering an opening bid.

‌



The 21-year-old is a regular for Club Brugge and forced his way into Belgium‘s World Cup squad, featuring in his country’s quarter-final defeat to winners Spain last month.

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

United did have Newcastle's Lewis Hall on their radar after the ex-Chelsea man had enjoyed the best season of his career to date, but the Magpies are refusing to sell up.

Already this summer Newcastle have lost marquee players in Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes. Hall is one of the leading lights and St James' Park bosses have refused to entertain his departure. United had ultimately been priced out whilst another target, young Spaniard Jorge Salinas, is poised to remain in La Liga.

‌



He reportedly remains fully committed to Racing Santander and "doesn’t want to leave" despite interest from Manchester and Barcelona. His manager Jose Alberto has grown tired with the incessant speculation regarding Salinas’ future during the summer window.

View 2 Images Lewis Hall had been a target for Man Utd (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

The left-back could be available for just €16m (£13.7m) due to a release clause in his contract at Racing, but his boss maintained that he and another of his in-demand team-mates want to remain. "They don’t want him to leave. And they show every day that they don’t either," he said.

‌



"But we know how this world works and there are release clauses. If a team comes along and pays the clause, they cease to be our players."

United currently have Luke Shaw as their first choice left-back, but he has struggled to remain fit throughout his career and, now into his 30s, the club are looking to future proof the position.

Sports.title: 'Everyone can have an opinion' - F1 president responds to regulations criticism
Sports.content:
Formula 1 president Stefano Domenicali says drivers "can have their opinion" and are not being stopped from criticising the sport's power unit regulations.

The 2026 technical regulations have divided opinion with Max Verstappen among those to voice his concerns about the rules which have led to a different style of driving and racing.

Verstappen has previously described the yoyo style of racing - which sees passes then re-passes - as "anti-racing" and joked at last month's Belgian Grand Prix that someone would "probably shoot me outside the door" if he criticised the rules.

The Red Bull driver clarified a week later in Hungary: "I've spoken my mind about these regulations already a long time, and in the beginning, most people were saying, 'ah, he's complaining; he should shut up'.

"But I have to say that the last few races, more and more people are seeing the same thing that I could see coming already a long time, and it's not about me not liking not winning anymore.

"It's just because I care about the product, and because I've said it many times, and at one point that's also enough, right? But of course, when people keep asking you, then yeah, maybe it's not appreciated always, but I'm just speaking. I'm just speaking my mind because you see certain things coming, and then sometimes people say, 'yeah, but this was a great race'.

"I say, 'yeah, but it's not really realistic the way we are racing'. And then you arrive to some tracks, and yeah, you're driving on not a lot of horsepower for F1 standards, and it's a little bit painful, which I could see coming already for years. It's then, of course, not the most exciting. But at one point, I'm also a little bit just fed up with repeating myself because it's already hard enough just having to drive it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton went wheel to wheel in a feisty scrap at the Austrian GP

Domenicali says he would prefer to discuss things behind closed doors to find solutions but respects all the drivers' opinions.

"You know me, we are not here to put tape on the mouth of anyone. The beauty of our sport is that everyone can have an opinion, but the opinion is an opinion," he said.

"There is someone who has the duty to have a line. There are certain drivers that prefer, of course, certain things. That in the process we have highlighted the need to be constructive in that respect."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen shocked Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Domenicali: F1 is bigger than any driver

In March, Verstappen stated he was considering his future in the sport if the regulations did not change for next year, such was his dissatisfactions with the new power unit rules which have more electrical power compared to previous seasons.

The current split is nearly 50-50 between internal combustion and electrical power but the FIA announced in May it had agreed with the teams to change this to 58-42 for 2027 and 60-40 for 2028.

Since then, Verstappen has not suggested he will walk away from F1, although questions remain over whether he will drive for Red Bull or another team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater assesses what Verstappen's next move could be and whether the Red Bull driver may head to McLaren or Mercedes

Domenicali said: "Max is an incredible driver. I've stated so many times that maybe I'm getting older to repeat that!

"Max is in a situation where if he loves Formula 1. We discuss together the regulations for the future. I have an incredible relationship with him.

"F1 is big enough for him to be part of us, but of course he will decide his future, the way that he prefers to do. The sport will look ahead but my opinion is that Max will stay with us, and I really hope so, and that's what I'm stating. The sport is big, much bigger than anyone else, all of us."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hamilton and Charles Leclerc went head-to-head in their Ferrari's at the Chinese GP

Every F1 event this season has been sold out with record crowd attendances in Australia (484,000), Canada (360,000), Austria (320,000), Silverstone (564,000), Belgium (400,000) and Hungary (310,000).

Domenicali pointed to the continued growth of F1 and a conversation he had with filmmaker and creator of Star Wars, George Lucas, which shows the majority of fans are "not interested in how you drive the car" but instead whether there is overtaking or not.

"I had an incredibly interesting discussion with George Lucas on Saturday. He was in Hungary, and he was giving me an incredible view on how the new fans are watching Formula 1," he said.

"He gave us an incredible clearance to see how we can really simplify things because the new fans are not understanding the truth, what is behind the scenes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard Alpine's Franco Colapinto as he pulls off an incredible double overtake on Pierre Gasly and Liam Lawson at the Belgian GP

"They are fascinated by the fact that there is a lot of action. There is definitely the need for those who are so focused on that to have the right information.

"But, for the vast majority of the people, trust me, they just want to see what is happening on the track, not interested in the angle of throttle or the percentage of brake pressure on how you can take and overtake a driver.

"For example, the incredible overtake of Max on Lewis at Turn 1 in Hungary, that was a piece of art, if I may say, that these people just want to see and just connect to the quality of the drivers."

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Ffos Las hosts six-race card
Sports.content:
Don't miss a moment from Ffos Las on Wednesday, with all six races live from 3.37pm on Sky Sports Racing.

4.37 Ffos Las - Narrjoo headlines following promising debut

Narrjoo headlines a field of seven in the Meyer Timber EBF Maiden Stakes.

Simon and Ed Crisford's representative finished second to exciting Godolphin newcomer Jassas when impressing on debut at Doncaster last month and will be tough to beat if he can run to the same standard. This 200,000gns son of Ten Sovereigns has future entries in the Champagne Stakes and Goffs Million, which indicate how highly he is thought of at Gainsborough Stables.

Drum Bay and Isabella de Vega both similarly caught the eye on their respective debuts, and should provide a good level of opposition to Narrjoo for Ralph Beckett and Ed Walker respectively.

The most intriguing newcomer comes in the form of the 200,000gns two-year-old Mehmas colt Engraved, who could run well first time up for the James Fanshawe team.

3.37 Ffos Las - No Half Measures' half-sister clashes with Eskimo Pie

Eskimo Pie seeks her first success in the Faucets The Bathroom Specialists Maiden Fillies' Stakes but will have to get past No Half Measures' half-sister Mystic Veil, who makes her debut.

Eskimo Pie finished a good seventh in the 2025 Queen Mary Stakes before running lame on her final start at two in the Princess Margaret. Her first start at three was promising, but she subsequently underperformed in her next two tries. She was bumped when looking to challenge at Newmarket the last day and very much sets the standard at her peak for the Jane Chapple-Hyam team.

The Ed Walker-trained Mollstar showed a respectable level of form on her third run before being found reportedly lame after her last start in December. Returning from a break here, this filly is an interesting contender under Ashley Lewis.

Mystic Veil is a half-sister to July Cup winner No Half Measures and is trained by Archie Watson - a handler renowned for his success with two-year-olds. She could very well succeed on her first outing and a market watch is essential in the build-up.

Dixie Blue - a daughter of Starspangledbanner - also makes her first start, while Livvy's Edge completes the quintet.

6.10 Ffos Las - Belle Of Kt bids for another success

Belle Of Kt bids for a hat-trick in the Dress For The Occasions Handicap, wish closes the card at the Welsh track.

The admirably consistent mare has found some improvement of late, putting a couple of wins together within the space of eight days. She did not seem to have loads in hand last time out when scoring by a nose, but should put up a bold effort when attempting a hat-trick, with Millie Wonnacott's 5lb claim potentially crucial.

A Daughters Love should prove tough to beat following a facile 10-length victory when bouncing back to form down in grade last time out. She clearly enjoys this course and distance but has been raised 6lb for that victory.

Noble Grace also won over course and distance just two weeks ago, yet in contrasting fashion, battling well in a terrific finish.

Sports.title: Jets' Stiggers in hospital after collapsing during practice
Sports.content:
New York Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers collapsed during a joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers; Stiggers regained consciousness and was talking on the field before being taken to hospital; Jets head coach Aaron Glenn later gave a positive update on Stiggers' condition

New York Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers was taken to a hospital by ambulance after he briefly lost consciousness during a joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Tuesday.

Jets coach Aaron Glenn said the 24-year-old was conscious and talking on the field before being put on a stretcher and taken for further examination. There was no immediate word on Stiggers' condition, but Glenn indicated the cornerback was doing okay.

"He was able to talk and I want to make sure I go and see him after this, just to make sure I'm good with everything," Glenn said. "But for the most part, he was good."

The Jets and Buccaneers were in the middle of special-teams drills when Glenn said Stiggers came to the sideline.

"He actually fell out," Glenn said. "The good thing is, he was conscious. Our guys did a hell of a job, just like most medical staffs around this league do in situations like that, and they took the necessary steps just to make sure that we do everything we can to be on board when it comes to those situations."

It was a somewhat scary scene, though, as several Jets team-mates took a knee near the sideline and some formed a prayer circle.

After several minutes, Stiggers was placed on a stretcher with what appeared to be an IV and loaded into the ambulance as fans seated near the area clapped in support.

"It was very sad, very emotional," Jets running back Breece Hall said. "You get on your knee and say a prayer for him and hope he's okay."

Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips added: "What's been shared to us is things are on the up and up."

Practice resumed after being halted for more than 10 minutes while Stiggers was being attended to.

Stiggers was earlier involved in one of the handful of chippy moments during the practice when he had his helmet flung down the field by a Buccaneers player after players on both teams scuffled.

Stiggers is entering his third season with the Jets after being a fifth-round draft pick in 2024. He was one of that draft's feelgood stories because he had no college football experience and was the first player drafted directly from the CFL, where he played for the Toronto Argonauts, since Miami took Jermaine Haley in 1999.

In 29 games, including five starts, with New York, Stiggers has 35 tackles, two fumble recoveries and three passes defended. He is also one of the Jets' top special teams players.

Sports.title: Super Giants rout SunRisers to move to cusp of Hundred eliminator
Sports.content:
Manchester Super Giants routed SunRisers Leeds to all but seal their place in The Hundred men's eliminator and leave their opponents at risk of being knocked out.

The Super Giants restricted SunRisers to 127 all out from their 100 balls as England's Gus Atkinson (3-30) and Sonny Baker (2-22) led the way, before opening batters Tim Seifert (80no from 40) and Paul Walter (44no from 28) knocked off the target with 33 balls to spare.

The huge margin of victory saw the Super Giants move above SunRisers into second place in the group table, with both sides on 20 points but Manchester having edged ahead on net run-rate. The result also confirmed Trent Rockets' place in Sunday's final as table-toppers.

Super Giants and SunRisers occupy the positions that would see them meet in Friday's eliminator for a place in the final, but can still technically be caught by fourth-placed MI London and fifth-placed Welsh Fire, who go into their final group-stage matches on Wednesday on 16 points, meaning wins would take them to 20 points.

While Welsh Fire's negative net run-rate of -1.001 makes it almost impossible they could catch either Super Giants or SunRisers when they face London Spirit, a big win for MI London away to Birmingham Phoenix could feasibly lift them into second or third.

Welsh Fire's clash with London Spirit is live on Sky Sports from 3pm, with MI London's trip to Edgbaston following at 6.30pm.

Asked whether he knew the net run-rate permutations ahead of the chase, Seifert, the Match Hero, said: "I had no idea, to be honest. A message got run out when we needed about 50 runs and that's when we looked to put the pedal down.

"We've got a great side and it's a great environment to play in. It's my first time playing in The Hundred and it's a great tournament to be involved in. It's great to be playing in front of good crowds in amazing stadiums."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Seifert hammered three sixes in a row!

Seifert bludgeoned his third fifty in as many knocks and struck seven sixes, while Walter thumped three maximums of his own as the SunRisers' attack was put to the sword.

The Super Giants' opening pair were electric but the foundations for a stunning win were laid by their bowlers, who clawed things back after Ryan Rickelton and Mitchell Marsh had made a rapid start for the visitors, posting 42 from 22 balls before Rickelton became the first of Atkinson's three victims.

Marsh (32 from 23), the tournament's leading run-scorer, continued his fine form, but when he was snaffled at extra cover off Noor Ahmad, the visitors lost their way.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A spectator was caught knitting at The Hundred!

Harry Brook, Dan Lawrence and Matthew Revis all fell cheaply and when Zak Crawley's stuttering innings of 31 from 28 was ended by Baker, the wheels came off.

SunRisers could only muster 14 runs from the final 14 balls of the innings, for the loss of four wickets. Expensive earlier in the piece, Atkinson was exceptional, taking two wickets and conceding just three runs from the final five.

Sports.title: SunRisers beat Super Giants to reach Hundred eliminator
Sports.content:
Reigning champions SunRisers Leeds snatched a spot in the women's Hundred eliminator by beating Manchester Super Giants by 41 runs in a winner-takes-all game at Old Trafford.

In a shoot-out for the final place in the top three, Annabel Sutherland's unbeaten 62 off 36 balls helped Leeds leapfrog their opponents and set up an eliminator clash against Southern Brave.

The Australian all-rounder hit nine boundaries, including three sixes, as the visitors posted 166-4 after being put in to bat.

Visiting spinner Jess Jonassen took 3-21, while Deepti Sharma and Sutherland claimed two wickets apiece, as Manchester were restricted to 125-8 in reply and exited the competition after slipping to fourth place in the standings.

Second-placed Leeds will continue their title defence against Southern Brave on Friday at The Oval, with table-topping Trent Rockets awaiting the winner in Sunday's final at Lord's.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player UNBELIEVABLE athletic fielding from SunRisers' Phoebe Litchfield to prevent a six

Sutherland, the Match Hero, said: "It's the beauty of being an all-rounder, you're in the game all the time, and I love competing, especially in a match we were calling a final. We had to win and it was nice to do a job for the team."

Phoebe Litchfield made her intentions clear after SunRisers were asked to bat, the Aussie opener racing to 27 from 12 deliveries to leapfrog Sophia Dunkley at the top of the competition's run-scoring chart.

An electrifying innings was brought to a halt after Litchfield miscued a drag down from Mady Villiers but Bryony Smith (17 off 16) and Lauren Winfield-Hill (20 off 15) kept the scoreboard ticking.

Sports.title: Levy goes up against Spurs owners to buy London's NBA Europe team
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham chairman Daniel Levy is vying with a consortium including current Spurs' owners, the Lewis family, to buy NBA Europe's London-based team.

Sky News has revealed that the Lewises are part of a consortium, led by the Checketts family, which has submitted an offer as part of the ongoing auction.

The Checketts have owned or invested in professional sports franchises including Major League Soccer team Real Salt Lake and the NHL's St Louis Blues.

The third leg of the consortium is the Eccles family, who own shares in Burnley FC and Spanish side Espanyol along with the Checketts.

Sky News has previously reported Levy's involvement in a consortium including Liberty Global and MSP Sports Capital, a former backer of McLaren Racing, which is also among the contenders for the NBA London team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh Solhekol examines where Daniel Levy was 'pushed' out of his role as Spurs chairman

London has rapidly become most highly prized of the 12 new NBA Europe outfits, with other teams based in cities such as Berlin, Manchester, Milan, Munich, Paris and Rome.

The NBA wants to generate billions of dollars by selling the rights to the teams, with the first transactions expected in the coming weeks.

Wealthy US families and investors are increasingly buying stakes in sports teams in the UK, especially in football.

Levy left his role as Spurs executive chairman in September 2025 after nearly 25 years in the job.

While the official communication from Spurs and Levy was that he had "stepped down" from the role, it was widely understood that the decision was taken out of his hands.

Sports.title: Floodlights to be on throughout Hundred matches for solar eclipse
Sports.content:
Floodlights will be turned on throughout games in The Hundred on Wednesday due to the solar eclipse.

Up to 90 per cent of the sun will be obscured by the moon during the eclipse, which will occur between 6.17pm and 8.06pm, peaking shortly after 7pm.

It will be the first partial solar eclipse for 27 years and will be visible across Europe, with some places experiencing a total eclipse, where the sun, moon and earth all line up in space.

The light will dim, the temperature will drop and the wind may change direction as the sun disappears behind the moon. After a few minutes the sun will reappear and daylight will return.

There are four games in The Hundred taking place on Wednesday, all of them live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Seifert & Walter hit 10 HUGE sixes in Super Giants win

Welsh Fire women face London Spirit women at 11.30am in Cardiff, followed by the men's game at 3pm. Birmingham Phoenix women host MI London at Edgbaston from 3pm before the men's teams play each other at 6.30pm.

In anticipation for the solar eclipse, organisers will keep floodlights on throughout all four matches and additional messaging will be issued to fans.

Experts have warned that only special solar eclipse glasses that are certified for the safest eye protection should be used to view the eclipse.

Floodlights will be on 'plenty early' at Kempton

Kempton is all set to stage racing on Wednesday during the solar eclipse.

While the twilight meeting at Ffos Las will begin and end earlier than originally scheduled to ensure all six races take place in daylight, there are no such issues at Kempton due to the floodlights that are in place at the Sunbury circuit.

Image: The floodlights will also be turned on at Kempton race course

The eclipse is expected to occur between 7.02pm and 7.16pm and Kempton has races scheduled to take place at 7pm and 7.30pm.

Kempton's clerk of the course Barney Clifford said: "The last one was nearly 30 years ago so I wasn't quite at Kempton then. I remember it but there were no floodlights in those days!

"I'm going to put the floodlights on early doors. I know they have predicted a time for it but you don't quite know how much of the sun is going to be covered and for what race so we'll have the lights on plenty early enough."
