Sports.title: Inter Milan in talks over Spurs and England defender Spence
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Inter Milan over the sale of Djed Spence.

Inter believe a total package of £30m could be enough to get a deal done and Spurs are understood to be willing to sell if they receive an acceptable offer.

Spence's opportunities could be limited at Spurs this season with Destiny Udogie and Andy Robertson also competing for the left-back position and the ever-present Pedro Porro the clear first choice on the right.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Spence's brilliant cameo off the bench against Norway, England fans Ben Cipolla and Dan Lucas came up with a new song for the full-back titled 'Total Eclipse of Djed Spence'

Inter want to bring in a new player who can operate as a wing-back.

Spence has been high on their list all summer and Inter are now turning their attention to the Spurs man after struggling to strike a deal for Al Ittihad's Moussa Diaby.

De Zerbi: Spurs aren't done in the transfer window

Roberto de Zerbi maintains Tottenham are "not finished yet" in the transfer market as they look to build a competitive Premier League squad again.

Having only avoided relegation on the final day of last season, Spurs have spent already spent around £237m - with the club's transfer record broken twice in deals for Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tottenham Hotspur head coach Roberto De Zerbi tells the Men in Blazers Network that he expects to make more signings this summer (Pictures: Men in Blazers Network)

Dutch defender Jan Paul van Hecke also arrived from Brighton for £52m, while Martin Dubravka, Robertson and Marcos Senesi signed on as free agents.

With Micky van de Ven having also committed his long-term future to the club, there is genuine hope Spurs will soon be challenging at the other end of the table.

"In the transfer market, we have not finished yet [with] the players who will arrive," De Zerbi said, speaking to the Men in Blazers Network.

"We are looking forward to start another season with, I don't know [different] ambitions, but with different results."

De Zerbi continued: "The club has been great because they closed [deals for] very, very important players. I think we have not finished yet.

"Okay, we spent money, but the other clubs made the same or more in the past. To compete in the Premier League, you need first [the] level of the players.

"The ambition of the owner of the club, of the board, of the people who decide behind me are very important and very high, so we have to find the condition to build a strong team, a stronger team than the last seasons, to compete again for the top of the table."

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 5: Brighton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 9th (NB: this is not necessarily John Brewin’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 8th

Prospects

Last season’s final day in May featured Brighton fans and players united in celebrating qualification for the Europa Conference League despite losing 3-0 to Manchester United. Considering West Ham and Crystal Palace have won the competition since its inception, lifting that trophy becomes a target to aim for.

How realistic is that? Beyond the Thursday-Sunday schedule playing in the Conference League demands, it has been a summer of change within the ranks. James Milner did not celebrate as Europe was reached. By then he had decided he would retire. Danny Welbeck was last season’s outstanding forward for Brighton, one of the best in England, and has followed the now traditional trade route to Chelsea. Him turning 36 in November adds a note of curiosity to that transfer. Thus, the veteran class, each older than their head coach, Fabian Hürzeler, still just 33, is reduced to Pascal Gross, Lewis Dunk and the reserve goalkeeper Jason Steele. Solly March not being offered a new contract was another break from the past, a surprise to a long-serving and popular player whose injury problems counted against him.

Jan Paul van Hecke, last season’s best defender, has been sold to Tottenham for £52m, with the teenager Luka Vuskovic coming in the opposite direction. If Brighton supporters are wondering about their club’s slew of new signings then their Premier League peers will be watching as closely, such is the industry’s respect for the club’s recruitment. The Jamestown Analytics company owned by Tony Bloom, Brighton’s financier, is a football Rosetta Stone, admired and coveted. It is not, though, completely infallible; there have been a number of busts.

Fans hugely enjoyed being in the Europa League three seasons ago, reaching the last 16, but it had a deleterious effect at home, stretching resources and relations with the then manager, Roberto De Zerbi. Brighton finished a disappointing 11th. Better is hoped for this time around.

Off-field picture

Safe standing is being expanded in the South Stand of the Amex, as part of a £40m modernisation project. The work will take place during September’s extended international break and is a drive towards enhancing the atmosphere. The ownership is among the most mindful of the matchday experience in English football. For Albion fans seeking a middle ground between the posh seats and pre-match drinks in the concourse, there’s the opening of the 1901 Pub, a “hybrid traditional pub and premium matchday lounge designed for a more relaxed fan experience”. With a capacity of 660, membership starts at £173 a month.

Owner-fan relationship

There can be no doubt that Brighton’s continued success relies on the patronage and funds of Bloom. The club’s supporters are more than aware of this. Last season, Bloom’s involvement with Hearts’ chase for the Scottish title demonstrated he has wider horizons, though his key priority will always be the hometown, boyhood club. In January, “the Lizard”, as he is known in the gambling circles he made his fortune, increased his Brighton investment with a £107m loan, making for an overall loan amount of £400m. Without Bloom’s financing and his continued enthusiasm, Brighton would not be the established, model Premier League force they remain.

The manager

Hürzeler has done much growing up in public. There have been points during his two seasons when doubts circled. In the boardroom, though, Bloom and his influential chief executive, Paul Barber, have kept faith in the still youthful Bavarian. As a new, three-year contract was announced in May, Bloom referred to a “clear playing identity”. Hürzeler can be fiery. His touchline behaviour does not always meet the approval of officials and opposing coaches but he enters the season as the fifth longest-serving manager in the Premier League and will be showing off a severe hair remodelling unveiled in pre-season. Success in European football can burnish a growing reputation.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen New arrival Luka Vuskovic’s playmaking abilities from the back are highly regarded. Photograph: Matt Impey/Shutterstock

Will Tottenham rue never drawing on Vuskovic’s potential? Brighton hope so. He never played a match for Spurs but impressed on loan at Hamburg, where his reading of the game, positioning and maturity drew rave reviews. The signing of the experienced centre-back Pascal Struijk from Leeds means Vuskovic can be allowed time to develop but the Croatian’s playmaking abilities from the back may make him a long-term successor for the captain, Dunk. His fee, reported at £46m when Spurs paid £12m for him, suggests the demand for his talents. The hope and expectation is that the deal becomes regarded as a bargain.

Stat attack

The two Manchester clubs were the only sides who scored more Premier League goals than Brighton in regular play last season. The Seagulls dropped down the standings a little once counterattacks were included but they had an identical rate for open play expected goals per game as Arsenal in 2025-26. There should be no shortage of chances for whoever picks up the goalscoring baton after Danny Welbeck’s departure.

Set for a breakthrough

Patience with new arrivals is part of the Brighton doctrines, players are given latitude and opportunity to bed in. A season’s grace is often granted, and Charalampos Kostoulas showed a few flashes of his talent during the 2025-26 campaign. With Welbeck departed, there is a vacancy to lead the line. The Greece international scored a brilliant overhead kick against Bournemouth in January, and at 19, last summer’s signing from Olympiakos should receive more airtime than the two league starts he received last season. His Greek compatriot Stefanos Tzimas, back in training after an ACL rupture, can provide either competition or a partnership.

World Cup impact

When Jordan Henderson played master of ceremonies as England celebrated third place at the World Cup, he made sure Steele was given a medal for his acclaimed, appreciated work as training goalkeeper. It was an otherwise mixed summer for Albion players, with Maxim De Cuyper going furthest to the quarter-finals with Belgium. Diego Gómez was suspended for Paraguay’s historic defeat of Germany though featured in his country’s bruising exit at the hands of France. Yasin Ayari became the first Brighton player to score two World Cup goals in a game as Sweden beat Tunisia 5-1. Michael Svoboda, the summer defensive signing from Venezia, did not play a single minute for Austria.

Sports.title: Infantino’s opponents developing new framework for running world football
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s opponents are working together to produce a new framework for running world football to replace what they regard as a system of patronage that Fifa has adopted since he replaced Sepp Blatter as president 10 years ago.

Repeated calls from Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation for an independent review of Fifa’s governance have been ignored by Infantino since his plan to sell off 21% of the World Cup was made public a fortnight ago, and the rebels are now understood to have taken matters into their own hands.

A source with knowledge of the discussions told the Guardian that the three confederations are working on producing a policy document to demonstrate how the world governing body could evolve in the future.

Those involved have been empowered to ask existential questions such as what Fifa’s precise role should be, how it should be structured and what governance model should be adopted. Financial distribution among member associations is also a key consideration, particularly with an eye on how best to deploy funds from Fifa’s estimated $5bn (£3.7bn) reserves.

If Infantino refuses to engage then the new framework is likely to be adopted by a challenger at the presidential election next year, or could even serve as a template for a breakaway organisation.

After releasing a joint statement on Monday, which called for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”, Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC let it be known that they have begun preliminary discussions about organising new competitions if the standoff with Fifa’s leadership persists.

View image in fullscreen Uefa officials are meeting in Salzburg where the Super Cup takes place on Wednesday between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa. Photograph: Gintare Karpaviciute/Reuters

At present the Under-20 Women’s World Cup next month could take place without European teams, as Uefa is maintaining that its members will boycott the tournament, unless Fifa moves quickly to set up an independent review of the World Cup sell‑off debacle and provide legally binding assurances that such a move will not be repeated.

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is seen as the most likely presidential challenger to Infantino at this stage – although, as he told the Guardian in June, his current focus is on being reelected as president of the North and Central American confederation next year.

It seemed significant, however, that the joint statement released on Monday contained strong echoes of a speech given by Montagliani at the Fifa congress this year in Vancouver, where he said: “Let me be frank, leadership is not about power.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Senior figures from European football are gathering in person for the first time since the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal broke, with a number of meetings expected in Salzburg – where the Uefa Super Cup final will be held on Wednesday – over the next two days.

The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, will hold talks with Nasser al-Khelaifi, the chair of European Football Clubs, aimed at reinforcing the continent’s unity in demanding a change at the top of Fifa.

Uefa continues to hold firm in its pledge to boycott Fifa competitions, having not received its desired assurances that there will be no recurrence of the issues that caused the current crisis.

Sports.title: Emery positive about Aston Villa’s outlook despite summer exits as PSG await
Sports.content:
One thing was almost instantly detectable as Unai Emery walked into a stuffy room inside the Red Bull Arena on the eve of Wednesday’s Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain. After a summer of change, Aston Villa’s manager appeared uber-relaxed, confident his team will absorb a series of headline departures. He cracked a joke about his English improving and poked fun at John McGinn, impersonating his captain while next to him on the auditorium’s top table.

Emery was in a jovial mood, then. But he was also switched on, alert to the frequency, the tone of the wave of questions at the beginning of his fourth full season in the job. “You ask about the changes of coaches and players, but McGinn is intelligent and his answer was fantastic,” Emery said with a smile. “When he arrived here [in 2018] they were in the Championship and every year since there have been changes and still the club has moved forward.

“If we compare ourselves to other clubs like Man City, Chelsea, Manchester United, Arsenal and Liverpool, we are competing with them. We don’t have their power … yet.”

Emery spoke with an enthusiasm that will be music to the ears of Villa supporters fretting about the size of the task on his hands. Villa have sold Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, the latter returning to PSG, for whom he could make his second debut against his former club. Villa would be tested again if Arsenal make a serious play for Ezri Konsa, who, together with Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martínez, remains on holiday after World Cup duty. Three key coaching staff have also left, including the set-piece coach, Austin MacPhee. But Emery, the beating heart of the operation, as McGinn said, is still in the building.

McGinn’s response was punchy when asked where expectations should be for the forthcoming campaign. “Similar to where it has been in the past few seasons,” he said. “I think we have consistently competed with the best in England, the best in Europe, no matter what the competition is. We will have our challenges. There is a lot of change, but when you look at other clubs around England there is a lot of change there as well: a lot of coaches changing, a lot of players changing.

“But what we still have is our main core, same manager, same methods, same desire to achieve more. A lot of people thought we had reached our ceiling a couple of seasons ago, and we proved them wrong. We have still got the same hunger and desire to go and achieve more. Our job is just to integrate the new players and try and make them believe, in the same way the players in the last few seasons have believed. I’m really excited by the sort of ‘new Aston Villa’.”

View image in fullscreen Players and staff of Aston Villa on the pitch at Stadion Salzburg. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Villa, of course, did not want to lose Rogers. Chelsea paid £117m to sign the England midfielder, two and a half years after Emery asked Villa to pay £8m to take him from Middlesbrough. The same goes for Tielemans, who after a slow start established himself as one of Emery’s undroppables. Villa signed Tielemans on a free but sold the 29‑year‑old for £35m. Digne was an equally reliable performer, taking back the left-back spot from £38m buy Ian Maatsen.

Emery knows the business but it was particularly interesting to hear him talk about the importance of the leverage Villa have gained off the back of the ride they have been on over the past few years. One of the most memorable nights was their pulsating quarter-final against PSG 16 months ago, a 3-2 second‑leg victory at Villa Park, when Gianluigi Donnarumma pulled off three superb saves to prevent Villa taking the game to extra time. Emery ended up on all fours after Willian Pacho blocked Maatsen’s goal-bound volley with 28 seconds to play.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The Premier League is the best league in the world and Aston Villa can now have better brands in the way we are,” Emery said. “I am so, so, so happy how the club is committed together with us. [I am so happy] with how we are getting better, keeping our consistency in the Premier League … the club is making a huge effort to try to be in the same direction as me. They are trying to extend Villa Park to achieve 50,000 supporters next season. We are increasing our budget through good results on the pitch, by sometimes selling some players and being consistent like we are, and as well expecting a high level, like we are more or less keeping.”

Emery, who spent two years in charge of PSG, knows how these things work. PSG are no longer just a football team but a brand: see their megastore on London’s Oxford Street. PSG’s chief executive, Victoriano Melero, has talked of PSG competing with the likes of Real Madrid on the pitch but labels like the LA Lakers and Ferrari off it.

Salzburg is the latest destination on Villa’s quest for success, with 6,000 Villa fans in tow. The stadium facade is plastered with images of McGinn and co celebrating their Europa League win in Istanbul in May. “I am feeling comfortable, happy, very demanding, even more than the last years,” Emery said. “We want more. We are not stopping here.”

Sports.title: Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to Manchester United as left-back solution
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to Manchester United as a potential left-back option, with Arsenal wishing to recoup some of the £75m paid to Newcastle for Bruno Guimarães.

Chelsea, it is understood, have also been made aware of the 19-year-old’s availability. Lewis-Skelly won the Premier League under Mikel Arteta last term, but whether the west London club will make a move for him is unclear.

Lewis-Skelly, who made only five league starts and 36 appearances in all competitions in 2025-26, signed a five-year contract last summer. His prospective price is thought to be in the region of £45m.

This is within the range of finance United have spent so far this summer, after Youri Tielemans’s £35m move from Aston Villa and Andrey Santos’s arrival for £48m plus £2m of add-ons from Chelsea. United are now weighing up a move for the teenager.

Newcastle’s Lewis Hall remains of prime interest for United but, after losing Guimarães, Sandro Tonali to Tottenham, and Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, the new Newcastle manager, Matthias Jaissle, is intent the 21-year-old England international does not also depart

RB Leipzig’s 28-year-old left-back David Raum is another in the position United may assess.

Chelsea have already had a busy summer in the market, having spent over £300m on a raft of new signings. Maxence Lacroix and Marco Palestra have been brought in to bolster the centre and right of the defence respectively, while Morgan Rogers became the club’s record signing at a cost of £117m.

But Xabi Alonso’s side have a hole on the left of their defence after Marc Cucurella’s £52m move to Real Madrid. The 20-year-old Jorrel Hato, who featured for the Netherlands at the World Cup, was Cucurella’s deputy at left-back.

Mason Mount missed training on Monday and Tuesday at United’s County Kildare summer training camp owing to a knock he received on a foot in Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg.

The the 27-year-old midfielder being stood down is a precautionary measure, it is understood, and he is also set to sit out Wednesday’s penultimate pre-season friendly against Leeds at Croke Park. The game at the 81,300 capacity venue is a sell-out.

United’s final friendly before Michael Carrick’s team start the season on Saturday week at Hull is against Milan in Wroclaw on Saturday.

Sports.title: Djed Spence nears Tottenham exit with Inter in talks over £25.6m move
Sports.content:
Tottenham are prepared to allow Djed Spence to join Inter, with the England defender expected to cost around €30m (£25.6m).

Spence – who started four games at the World Cup, including the semi-final against Argentina – has fallen further down the pecking order at Spurs after the arrival of Andy Robertson from Liverpool. He signed a new four‑year contract in north London at the start of last season but is believed to be keen on joining the Italian champions, with Destiny Udogie and Pedro Porro expected to be Roberto De Zerbi’s preferred full‑backs this season.

Talks are ongoing over a fee for the 26-year-old as Inter search for a replacement for Denzel Dumfries, who joined Real Madrid this summer. But personal terms are not believed to be an issue and an agreement is likely to be reached that will see Inter pay only slightly more than the £20m fee Spurs paid to sign Spence from Middlesbrough in 2022.

Inter also held talks with Tottenham over a potential move for Cristian Romero but the Argentina defender looks poised to join Atlético Madrid for a fee of €40m. They have yet to agree a fee but Romero is expected to move to La Liga despite interest from elsewhere, including the Premier League champions Arsenal.

On Monday, Spurs – who have spent almost £240m this summer on new players, including Sandro Tonali for a club‑record £92.5m, confirmed that Micky van de Ven has signed a new five-year contract. “It’s clear the direction the club wants to go in and I want to be a part of it. I’m excited about what’s to come,” the Netherlands defender said.

Crystal Palace, meanwhile, are in talks to re-sign Evann Guessand on a season-long loan from Aston Villa. The Côte d’Ivoire forward spent the second half of last season at Selhurst Park and was part of the side that won the Conference League in May, although Palace decided not to take up an option to sign him earlier in the summer. The south London club are also expected to complete deals for Anan Khalaili from Union Saint‑Gilloise for £21m and Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake for £11m.

Sports.title: ‘I am quite optimistic’: Newcastle’s Jaissle on leading club after turbulent summer
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle has been described as “fire” and a “rockstar”, but his formal “unveiling” as Newcastle’s manager revealed a rather more considered and conservative character than advertised.

At the precise moment the clock struck 3pm on Tuesday the 38‑year‑old German walked into a packed media suite at St James’ Park. Before taking his seat on the stage Jaissle, wearing a smartly understated open-necked suit complete with a silk pocket square, took a deep breath and jumped down into audience, making a point of shaking everyone’s hand. It was a courteous and classy gesture.

Once back on that podium, his evident excitement at exchanging Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli for the Premier League was tempered by the sort of realism inevitable at a club that, in Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães, has just sold its three best players.

“This is now a vacuum as you call it,” Eddie Howe’s successor said in his excellent English. “They were great characters, great players, ­experienced players. Obviously we are in that transition phase. My job is to make the best out of it all. I am quite optimistic. We are ambitious, that’s the most important thing and why I decided to come here. But it will not happen overnight. I’m pretty sure it will be a successful story. But we need time now.”

Regular chats with the England head coach, Thomas Tuchel, promise to help minimise any culture shock. “It’s been a long connection,” he said. “Thomas was my youth coach when I was a youth player at Stuttgart. He was amazing, I really admire him.

“He’s a really special coach and I’m looking forward to staying in touch with him, and getting insights on the league. That’s something I want to use for sure. But it’s also important to build your own opinions because every coach is their own human being and has their opinions and, ­sometimes players get stuck in a box. It’s ­important for me to be neutral about players.”

Allied to a willingness to chall­enge assumptions, such refusal to take labels at face value hinted at the qualities that prompted David ­Hopkinson, Newcastle’s Canadian chief executive, to dub Jaissle “fire” and “a rock star”.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle beat Valencia 2-1 in Jaissle’s first pre-season game in charge. Photograph: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images

If the one-time RB Salzburg manager’s brand of football – “front foot, intense, aggressive, vertical and, of course, also successful” – fits the latter tag, Newcastle fans have greeted him with an adaptation of a late 1970s Euro-disco hit.

Where the Spanish female pop duo Baccara soared to No 1 with Yes, Sir I Can Boogie, travelling supporters attending the friendly win in Valencia last Saturday chorused: “Oh Jaissle I can boogie/You try me once, you’ll beg for more.”

Jaissle said: “All my staff members already said they’re looking forward to sitting after a match in the bar and listening to the song. So let’s see about that! I heard it once and I was smiling. I’m really happy the fans already appreciate me a lot. The welcome from the fans was unbelievable when I was having a walk yesterday in the city. It was really giving me a nice feeling.”

There were more “big smiles” when he recalled a phone call last month asking him if he would be interested in replacing Howe but, little more than 48 hours after arriving in Newcastle for the first time following a training camp at La Manga in southern Spain, Jaissle is under no illusions as to the scale of the challenge ahead.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With the need to comply with football’s spending rules having seen the club pivot to buying young players with high resale potential – four of their five summer signings so far are aged 20 or younger – the immediate future remains opaque.

“I’m long enough in the industry now that you cannot promise anything,” Jaissle said when asked what he aimed to achieve this season. “It makes no sense to promise you things now because I don’t know how things will look in one year. But it doesn’t make sense to see the negative. There will be more adjustments to the squad this summer. We still have time. I would say keep the optimism.”

His cautiously upbeat mood will be bolstered further should Newcastle’s ongoing talks with Benfica about potentially signing their 23‑year‑old full-back Amar Dedic, who played for Jaissle at Salzburg and can operate on both the right and the left, conclude successfully.

“I had a tour of St James’ Park two days ago,” Jaissle said. “When I entered the pitch here with my assistant coaches for the first time, we were looking at each other with smiles and goosebumps. It’s really special, an amazing stadium. I can’t wait to see it full.

“When I received the call at the end of July and it was clearly most likely Eddie would quit there were no doubts or question marks. I had a big smile.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Liverpool, Jeff Bezos and mission creep off the field at Anfield
Sports.content:
THIS MEANS MORE (MONEY)

Far be it for Football Daily to make cheap gags [wait, what? – Football Daily Ed] relating to the involvement of Amazon founder and master of the universe Jeff Bezos in a consortium buying around 30% of Liverpool FC. Will new signings arrive via prompt delivery but end up next door at Everton? How will fans rate the packaging? Etc, etc. There’s also the involvement of Eduardo Saverin, the Facebook co-founder poking his head in. Though long ago unfriended by Mark Zuckerberg, Saverin still ranked No 56 on Forbes’s billionaires list. These are seriously rich men, and among the planet’s chino class, to quote Vladimir Putin, “soccer is popular”. The Geopolitics World Cup posh seats were full of those eyeing up deals on a frontier hardly new to investors from the USA USA USA, but where there may be much more gold to strike. See Gianni Infantino’s misreading of the art of the deal as an, ahem, prime example.

Bezos is no football man, barely known as a sports fan. Links with buying the Seattle Seahawks, his local NFL franchise, were speculative. He is, though, the third richest man in the world, according to appendage-measuring listicles. Amazon’s market value is higher than Brazil’s annual GDP. For certain people, that triggers arousal at the thought of their team being able to buy the biggest and best players in the world. Just imagine if their club was to spend, say, £446m in a single summer. How good would that be?

For others, there is a regrettable mission creep towards a civic institution – one that, despite global fame, cleaves to its local community – being tossed around by venture capitalists. Though that process has been in train since Tom Hicks and George Gillett arrived on Merseyside, full of huckster charm, almost two decades ago. The socialism and collectivism Bill Shankly envisaged for the club he made famous disappeared in the sepia-tinged rearview mirror. Football was a business even back in Shanks’ day but now attracts the richest suits of all; if Bezos is chancing his arm in football, what price Elon Musk or Google tycoon Larry Page are seen wearing the scarf of their chosen club? Oh joy.

Current overlords Fenway Sports Group, who picked up the pieces from impending disaster in 2010, are, yes, a consortium of American venture capitalists. Their existential aim is to make as much loot as possible from an asset purchased for a knockdown price of £300m. It’s gone well. This mooted deal includes Bezos, Saverin and Amit Bhatia, a frontman you may recognise from when QPR fans celebrated their owners being richer than Roman Abramovich. That did not go well. The latest deal would value the club at £4.4bn. High-fives all round, though the doubles and trebles may take time. Liverpool enter the season with an imbalanced squad, unsuited to a manager whose arrival was generally seen as a Good Thing. If football is all about money, even the biggest money cannot solve every problem.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“After careful consideration, we don’t feel it is right to proceed at this time without the necessary preparation in place, but we will remain in conversation with the club and see what is possible in the future” – one wealthy benefactor not entering the game – yet – is Turki Alalshikh, whose bid to buy a controlling interest in Derby will no longer proceed, with the club now off the market.

RECOMMENDED LOOKING

Here’s David Squires on … the masochistic life of a Football League fan.

View image in fullscreen Illustration: David Squires/The Guardian

double quotation mark Having also boycotted the GWC and also being very concerned about the season to come, I sympathise with Ken Muir (yesterday’s Football Daily letters). But at least Hearts know who their manager is. Due to the absurd, months-long FA ‘investigation’ into the manager who’s clearly admitted culpability for the undisputed facts of Spygate, my club, Southampton, is in a horrid limbo. Surely it could have been done and dusted in a couple of weeks and Saints could have planned accordingly. But perhaps the FA blazers were too busy writing their letter of support to Gianni Infantino to worry about destabilising my football club” – Bob Cushion.

double quotation mark ‘It’s 15 years of frustration here at this club,’ says Rangers boss Derek McInnes (yesterday’s Quote of the Day.) Steven Gerrard and the sole object in his managerial trophy cabinet would like a word, Derek” – David Maddock.

double quotation mark Given the surfeit of the recent GWC machinations, the blatherings and canvassing for Gianni to do one (or not) and the less-than-sportsmanlike attitude from members of the Argentina team, can we please have a reprise of the Football Daily’s erstwhile, eventually abortive, attempt to ‘STOP FOOTBALL’? It has to be worth a thought, before VAR, PGMOL and Arsenal’s Dark Arts Department™ get to work on the 2026-27 Premier League shenanigans, surely?” – Budgie Wright.

Sports.title: Chelsea face Real Sociedad in WCL third qualifying round with riches at stake
Sports.content:
Chelsea will face Real Sociedad in the Women’s Champions League third qualifying round, needing a win over two legs to secure a place in the main league phase of the competition.

The 2021 runners-up and six-time European semi-finalists are taking part in the qualifying stage by virtue of their disappointing third-placed finish in the Women’s Super League last season – their lowest league ­finish since 2019 – and they will be the favourites against the Spanish side.

Chelsea could have faced Ajax, Inter, Eintracht Frankfurt or the ­Austrian side St Pölten. They were unable to meet the big-name sides such as Real Madrid, Wolfsburg, Juventus or Paris Saint-Germain at this stage because of seedings. Sonia Bompastor’s team will hope to join Arsenal and Manchester City in the main phase of the competition.

The potential financial implications of missing out on ­qualification are significant. All 18 clubs that take part in the league phase will receive a guaranteed minimum of €505,000 (£431,500), plus a further €60,000 for every league‑phase fixture they win and €20,000 for every draw, as well as prize money ranging from €10,000 to €180,000 depending on where they finish in the table, rising by €10,000 per position.

Additionally, the eventual champions will receive €1,050,000 in prize money across the course of the knockout phase – including €500,000 specifically for winning the final – as there are six-figure sums on offer for each knockout-phase fixture.

Chelsea will be at home for the first leg, which is scheduled to be played on 26 August, with the second leg in Spain scheduled for 2 September, three days before Chelsea’s WSL season opener, which is at home against Aston Villa on 5 September.

Chelsea have been strong contenders for the European title in recent years, reaching the semi-finals in three of the past four campaigns, but they lost to their rivals Arsenal in a dramatic quarter-final last term.

Real Sociedad, based in San Sebastián, finished third in Spain’s top division last season behind Real Madrid and Barcelona. The ­qualifying draw was split into two sections, with a “champions path” for winners of their domestic divisions drawn ­separately to the “league path” which contained domestic runners-up and third-placed sides such as Chelsea.

Køge, who eliminated the Scottish champions Hearts earlier in the ­qualification process, were pitted against PSV, while in the most eye-catching tie of the round Ajax will take on Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Kyle Walker lined up for shock Premier League return
Sports.content:
Everton are reportedly considering a move for Kyle Walker.

The Burnley right-back has 12 months remaining on his deal at Turf Moor having joined the club from Manchester City last summer.

3 Walker (right) could do little to prevent Burnley from slipping into the Championship last season Credit: Getty



Walker, who has come close to joining Everton on multiple occasions during his career, could finally land at Hill Dickinson Stadium this summer.

The 36-year-old has continued to show his reliability having started 35 times in the Premier League for the Clarets in last season’s relegation campaign.

And he showed that he can still be decisive by netting Burnley’s winning penalty in Saturday’s Carabao Cup win over Notts County.

The move would provide Walker with another welcome shot at Premier League football despite his summer preparation for Championship football.



The Sun reports that Everton boss David Moyes is keen to bring in Walker, who boasts a wealth of experience ahead of a busy campaign for the Toffees with European qualification among the club’s objectives.

The right-back position is an area of concern for Moyes who has deployed centre-back Jake O’Brien as a make-shift full-back.



Everton are facing up to life without Seamus Coleman who left the club last summer while Nathan Patterson has failed to cement himself as a credible long-term successor to the Irishman.

Moyes will be hoping to fill the gap in time for their clash against Crystal Palace on the opening weekend of the season.



Moyes' shopping spree

The Everton boss has already been active in this summer’s transfer window with the additions of Christian Norgaard, Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Merlin Rohl.

Everton tied up to the signing of Brennan Johnson from Crystal Palace on Tuesday as part of a swap deal that saw Dwight McNeil move in the opposite direction.

3 Walker was almost an ever present in the Premier League for Burnley last season, clocking up 35 games Credit: Getty

After completing his switch to the Merseyside club, Johnson said: “I’m so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it’s a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.



“There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in.

“You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I’m a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

“I want to come in and show what I can do. The manager spoke to me about getting back to the form that I’ve shown previously, and that’s a massive thing for me – the fact he knows and believes in what I can do...

“For me, listening to him – a manager who is so experienced and someone who has been so successful – it was really nice to hear.



“I want to bring all of my attributes. First and foremost, I’ll work for the team, the fans, and represent the Club properly.

3 Everton can call upon Brennan Johnson after the Wales international sealed his switch from Crystal Palace Credit: Getty

“I know that’s something that’s definitely appreciated and a non-negotiable here. They can expect that from me. On top of that, I think I can bring speed, goals and everything I’ve got.

“The incredible fanbase that Everton has, whether it’s home or away, is something I’ve always felt. It’s a massive honour to be here and play for them now.”

Sports.title: I’ve never disliked a club captain more but this is why Arsenal transfer can’t happen
Sports.content:
I’ve never disliked a club captain more but this is why Arsenal transfer can’t happen

Cristian Romero can dream of a move to Arsenal but in reality, it’s a transfer that will never be sanctioned.

That’s the view of talkSPORT’s Abbi Summers who has never hidden her disapproval of the Spurs captain.

5 Romero's antics have at times angered Abbi Summers Credit: Getty

Summers has issued multiple passionate rants pertaining to the Argentine’s succession of controversial incidents both on and off the pitch.

talkSPORT understands Romero is set to join Atletico Madrid despite Tottenham initially agreeing a £34million deal with Napoli.

Meanwhile, Inter Milan held talks with the defender earlier this summer.

However, shock reports could point to an almighty twist in the future of Romero with recent suggestions that bitter rivals Arsenal could be ready to swoop for Romero has sparked Summers into yet another rant on the Spurs skipper.

The Gunners are reportedly open to bolstering their back line with William Saliba set for an extended spell on the sidelines due to a back injury.

The idea of Romero, who is under contract until 2029, moving to Arsenal instantly brings back memories of Sol Campbell’s infamous move across the north London divide in 2001 which still haunts Tottenham fans 25 years later.

Does Summers believe Romero would entertain a move to Arsenal?

“I don’t know him personally, he could be the nicest bloke in the world but I can only judge him as a footballer and the type of character I see on the pitch,” Summers said of Romero on her new talkSPORT YouTube channel.

“And yeah, I could see that actually being something he’d be open to. Why wouldn’t you want to go to the champions, let’s be honest?”

“He clearly doesn’t have any love, care or respect for Spurs in my opinion. I don't feel like I've ever seen that from him.

“It’s always been Argentina first, Spurs second.”

5 Summers says Romero lacks respect for Spurs whilst pouring all his passion into playing for his country Credit: Getty

Despite that, Summers is not convinced that a move to Arsenal would ever be a realistic opportunity for the Argentine.

“I cannot see a world where Tottenham would ever sanction a move,” she added.

“We’re not just talking about a young player here. We’re talking about a senior player who is the club captain crossing the divide, going to Arsenal.

“I cannot see a world where Tottenham, the hierarchy – even though I don’t think much of them – I just don’t think that they would allow that to happen.

“Let’s be honest, if that actually occurred and he went and played for Arsenal, imagine what that would be like in a north London derby.

“I don’t even know if he’d be able to enter Tottenham High Road. I don’t even know if he’d be able to enter the stadium.

5 Sol Campbell was subjected to a tyrant of abuse following his switch to Arsenal Credit: Getty

“I think where we’re so deeply traumatised and scarred by the Sol Campbell stuff, you can’t let your captain or any player go to Arsenal.

“I wouldn’t care if he went to Man United, Man City or somewhere else but we’re talking about a club like Arsenal.

“It’s the same with Chelsea. Spurs don’t do business with Chelsea, we don’t do business with Arsenal and we're certainly not going to allow the club captain, even if that’s what he wants, to make that move.”

No fee would be enough to sell Romero to Arsenal

Summers even claimed that a nine-figure sum would not be enough to tempt Spurs into strengthening their rivals ahead of next season’s title defence.

“It doesn’t matter if Arsenal offered me £100million. You cannot in principle let the captain of your football club go to your biggest rivals.

“I don’t really care what he goes for, I just want him away from the club but I do care that the location is not Arsenal.

5 Summer can usually be seen with this kind of expression when talking about Romero

“I think he would be a perfect fit for someone like Cheslea. I think Romero as a player is so Chelsea coded but I still wouldn’t want him to go to Chelsea.

“If it was other Premier League side’s out of those two I wouldn’t really care.”

And while Summers admitted that Romero does pose world-class attributes at times, she concluded with a message for La Liga’s two interested parties.

“I can understand why any club would want him even with the disciplinary record and the headloss,” she said

“It can be beaten out of someone in a way and I think playing in a different team with different standards which I do believe are set not only by the manager but also the captain.

“They set the standards. He was the one setting the standards. He was also late to training.

5 Roberto De Zerbi is already planning for life after Romero Credit: Getty

“Look at the mentality of what has gone on at my football club over the last couple of years compared to other football clubs.

“When the standards and the bar is so low, that is felt around everywhere and it’s not a surprise that Spurs were in a relegation battle and finished 17th two seasons in a row.

“If Atletico or Barca want a player that is extremely hotheaded, temperamental, unpredictable. Please be my guest.

“I’ve never disliked a club captain I don't think and I’m actually really excited for the new season because I feel it's a fresh start.”

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo confirms he and Georgina Rodriguez are married in candid post
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo confirms he and Georgina Rodriguez are married in candid post

Cristiano Ronaldo has officially tied the knot with long-time partner Georgina Rodríguez.

The Portuguese superstar got married to model Rodríguez in a civil ceremony on Tuesday.



4 Ronaldo and Rodriguez wed in a private ceremony Credit: Instagram

The ceremony took place in Cascais, Portugal a year to the day since the pair, who share two children together, announced their engagement on Instagram in 2025.

"Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife," a representative for the Al Nassr star said.

"The ceremony was a private and intimate moment attended by their five children."



Ronaldo took to Instagram once again to announce that the two had officially wed, posting a picture of the couple holding hands with their wedding bands with the caption: "C❤️G."

The wedding took place just days after it was believed that they would be tying the knot in Funchal Cathedral - Ronaldo's hometown - leading to thousands of fans gathering outside of the church.



How did Ronaldo and Rodríguez meet?

The two met back in 2016 when Argentine-Spanish Rodríguez was working at a Gucci store in Madrid.

In her Netflix documentary entitled 'Soy Georgina' (I am Georgina), the 42-year-old revealed that their meeting came by chance as she was supposed to leave work earlier that day, only to be asked to assist a special VIP client - Ronaldo, then playing for La Liga giants Real Madrid.



"I was finally able to leave the shop to go home three hours later than I should have and as I was getting ready to leave Cristiano came in with his eldest son and some friends," she shared in the documentary," she said.

"Let's just say it was butterflies in my stomach."

After that meeting, the two have been virtually inseparable, with Ronaldo often picking her up from work in his Bugatti after she had arrived via bus.

4 The two announced they had wed on Tuesday Credit: Instagram

4 Ronaldo has been with Rodriguez since 2016 Credit: Getty



"He would come, I remember once, once in a Bugatti. My co-workers went crazy. They get there on the bus, and I would leave in a Bugatti. I mean people couldn't believe it," she added.

It wasn't long before she had to quit her job at the store because of crowding.

But their relationship remained strong with Rodriguez taking on the role of parenting the three children Ronaldo had (Cristiano Jr, Eva Maria and Mateo) before meeting her.

Ronaldo and and Rodriguez share two children together, daughters Alana Martina and Bella Esmeralda.



Ronaldo must now feel that 'click'

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner also revealed during the documentary that he hadn't yet put a ring on Rodríguez's finger because he hadn't felt the special 'click'.

'I always tell her, 'when we get that click'. Like everything with our life, and she knows what I'm talking about," Ronaldo said.

4 Rodriguez been by Ronaldo's side over the last ten years with their life currently in Saudi Arabia Credit: Getty

'It could be in a year or it could be in six months or it could be in a month. I'm 1000 per cent sure that it'll happen.'



At the same time, Rodríguez admitted that her friends would always joke with her about when the wedding was.

"They're always joking about the wedding. 'When is the wedding?'" Rodríguez said.

"Since Jennifer Lopez's song The Ring or When came out, they started singing it to me. And well, this is not up to me."

Now it's finally happened.

Sports.title: Liverpool told to sign £60m-rated defender offered to Chelsea and Manchester United
Sports.content:
Liverpool should sign Myles Lewis-Skelly to compete with Milos Kerkez at left-back.

That's the view of Peterborough United owner and Reds fan Darragh MacAnthony amid uncertainty over the 19-year-old's Arsenal future.

4 Lewis-Skelly faces an uncertain future at boyhood club Arsenal Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that Lewis-Skelly has been offered to other Premier League clubs including rivals Manchester United and Chelsea.

The news comes after Arsenal completed the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle last week.

Although he has mostly played as a left-back, Lewis-Skelly is a midfielder by trade throughout his senior Arsenal career.

However, Guimaraes has joined strong midfield competition in Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino.

Lewis-Skelly made just five Premier League starts last season, and a move away may therefore offer more minutes from the off.

How much is Lewis-Skelly worth?

Reacting to the news on talkSPORT with Max Scott, MacAnthony said: "I love him, I think he's a great, young player."

"Why has he not been offered to Liverpool?" he asked, before adding: "Someone said, 'What's he worth?'

"I said, 'Anywhere from £40-60million for a player of that age that's English.'"

Scott then asked MacAnthony if he would welcome Lewis-Skelly at Liverpool this summer.

Kerkez is set to be the first-choice left-back in the new season ahead of Kostas Tsimikas, who is understood to want to fight for his place.

4 MacAnthony would love to see Liverpool make a move for Lewis-Skelly Credit: Getty

4 He wants the club to bring in competition for Kerkez Credit: Getty

"All day long," MacAnthony said: "We need competition for our left-back. No disrespect to Tsimikas, but not for me. And, he can play in midfield, we've seen him play in that role in midfield..."

When it was suggested that Lewis-Skelly's strongest position is in midfield, despite his experience at left-back, he replied: "Correct.

"Liverpool are crying out for that type of player who's got those defensive skills but also still has, technically, the attacking ability as well."

What could Lewis-Skelly be thinking?

Lewis-Skelly has been at Arsenal since the age of eight and worked through the academy ranks to feature in the first team.

He has already made 75 senior appearances for the north Londoners and won a Premier League title.

Whilst an exit is certainly not confirmed with Guimaraes' arrival, it does raise questions over whether or not he has a place in the team.

4 Lewis-Skelly has been praised for his versatility on the pitch Credit: Getty

"I know that you look at the game from the perspective of an owner and a businessman, and you can sometimes, sort of, remove yourself from the emotion of the game, and understandably so," Scott said to MacAnthony.

"But if you're Myles Lewis-Skelly, an Arsenal fan brought through the academy, you proved yourself last season, broke back into the team, been an integral part, and now you're hearing you're offered to other Premier League clubs...

"Is that just the ruthlessness of the game, or can you understand he might be frustrated by it?"

"I don't know where the report has come from, but I would imagine the player and his agent would know," MacAnthony responded. "So, they'd be aware, I'm sure this hasn't come out as a surprise on them.

"Maybe he wants to play more football, how many times did he play last year? I know he was in the Champions League final, I know he played a good few games at the end of the season.

"Maybe at that age, 19, 20, they want to go Man United and they want to go and play every week. We know United need that type of player, there's no doubt about it.

"They were in for (Lewis) Hall at Newcastle, I think the price of that was probably too expensive.

"This is a young, English talent who will be in the England team for years to come, so it's sensible business for whoever gets him."

Sports.title: Man United urged to go all-in for Premier League defender who wants to leave club
Sports.content:
Man United urged to go all-in for Premier League defender who wants to leave club

Djed Spence to Manchester United?

It’s a no-brainer according to Manchester United fan and talkSPORT host Flex.

4 Spence is being courted by Inter Milan but should Man United be in for the England man? Credit: Getty

The Tottenham defender was among England’s standout performers at the World Cup despite garnering detractors over his inclusion in Thomas Tuchel’s 26-man squad.

The 26-year-old silenced the doubters with a host of superb displays during the Three Lions’ run to the semi-finals.

But despite his heroics in North America, Spence’s future at Tottenham is unclear with the player understood to be open to a move away from the club.

Serie A champions Inter have been long-standing admirers of the full-back.

talkSPORT reported on Tuesday that the Nerrazzuri had reopened talks with Tottenham over signing him.

However, what may come as a surprise to many is the projected fee of around £25-30million that could see Spence land in Milan.

Spurs have spent heavily this summer with over £200m splashed on reinforcements and the club’s transfer record smashed twice in the same window.

Therefore, the north London club may need to offload some talents to balance the books and Spence could be at the top of the list.

A good fit at Old Trafford?

But Flex is hoping Inter won’t have an easy path to obtaining Spence’s signature and admits that Manchester United would benefit from the star’s skill set.

“This is one we need to be all over,” he told talkSPORT.

4 Spence was in sensational form for England at the World Cup Credit: Getty

“I’m sorry, we need to raise our ceiling of players we need to choose from.

“Not everyone has to be the number one starter or the left-back or right-back for the next ten years. You can’t always sign that player.

“But for where we are and the depths of the competitions we want to go into, stylistically I need different options.”

Conceding defeat

Flex was more than happy to take his own dose of humble pie after watching Spence’s World Cup performances.

“Djed Spence, I gave him a rough time. I’ll hold my hands up,” he added.

“Going into the World Cup when he was in the squad and there was no Trent [Alexander -Arnold] and no Lewis Hall and I saw people like Dan Burn and Djed Spence, I was like ‘what is this?’

4 Spence could be available for just £30m this summer Credit: Getty

“But he bit down on his gum shield and said I’m here to show people what I’m about. He didn’t play too dissimilar to how he actually plays.

“He’s very good in 1v1 situations, he’s extremely quick and can play on both sides.

“You’re talking about value in the market, I’d absolutely have him for £25million.”

Flex admits that a move for the Tottenham star might split the fan base but says that he could be prove to be a better option United’s current right-back choices.

“Some fans might question, he’s a right-back, we need a left-back out and out. I’d argue we need a right-back too,” he said.

“I’d argue he’s a potential upgrade on [Noussair] Mazraoui and Diego Dalot and have different styles.

4 Noussair Mazraoui could find his place under threat if United were to go all-in for Spence Credit: Getty

“Mazraoui is a very good footballer with his feet, with his understanding of the game, positionally.

“Going forward, less so but he’s a steady footballer and a very good squad guy to have.

“But, I’d have Djed Spence all day.”

Sports.title: Why Everton are the clear winners in Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil swap deal
Sports.content:
Why Everton are the clear winners in Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil swap deal

Everton have pulled off daylight robbery with a straight swap deal involving Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson.

The two clubs announced on Tuesday morning that McNeil is heading to Selhurst Park, with Johnson making the move to Hill Dickinson - without Everton having to fork out a single penny.

4 Johnson's time at Palace was short lived Credit: Getty

On paper, it is a move that does not immediately make sense, especially considering Palace made Johnson their club-record £35million signing just six months ago.

The 25-year-old has struggled badly since moving to south London, failing to score in 26 appearances for the Eagles.

However, both financially and statistically, Everton are getting the far better end of the bargain.

Speaking on talkSPORT on Monday, Ben Jacobs explained the situation: "It appears quite damaging for Crystal Palace’s books, but it’s a good old-fashioned swap deal.

"It’s probably the first time it’s happened between two Premier League clubs where there doesn’t appear to be any cash changing hands.

"I agree it’s a surprise, because Brennan Johnson, prior to Strand Larson arriving, was briefly Crystal Palace’s record signing.

"Whereas McNeil has a lower market valuation. He thought he was going in January, only to find there was a last-minute paperwork issue which disappointed him at the time.

"But he was sold on that move, personal terms agreed on a four-year contract. They have now been given permission to start their medicals this morning. This will be one going one way, one going the other in a straight swap deal.

"It does feel like, on paper and financially, the deal to gain Johnson is the better one. But I think Palace would argue that Johnson hasn’t worked out there, and the club has always wanted McNeil."

Everton would never have possessed the financial muscle to purchase Johnson in a standalone transaction had they simply pocketed the £20m Palace originally offered for McNeil in January.

4 McNeil saw a deadline day transfer to Crystal Palace from Everton fall through at the 11th hour in January Credit: Getty

Instead, Everton have made Palace effectively take a £15m hit under the Premier League's new squad cost ratio rules.

Both players must be valued at the same figure for the exchange, and when McNeil's proposed move to Selhurst Park fell through in February, he was valued at £20m.

If this is a true swap deal, and the two players are both valued at £20m, it will represent a £15m loss for Palace.

Will Johnson prove a success for Everton?

His tenure at Selhurst Park was undeniably underwhelming, drawing heavy criticism toward the 25-year-old.

On talkSPORT, Gabby Agbonlahor questioned the deal: "When I saw it, I was like 'I get it'. Certain managers and certain players suit one another. Maybe David Moyes is looking at it an wants more pace in the side, wanting to use him in that way.

"Also, with Dwight McNeil, there was talk he was leaving in January, and the new [Palace] manager has clearly seen enough of him already and wants to bring him in."

4 Johnson scored the only goal in the 2025 Europa League final to win the trophy for Spurs Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Jamie O'Hara replied: "Brennan Johnson has been a myth for a few seasons. He didn’t do it at Spurs. In one of our seasons he got top scorer, but he hides in big games."

Agbonlahor pointed out: "You look at both of them and their output last season - 16 Premier League appearances for Spurs, two goals, zero assists. Then at Palace, zero goals and one assist.

"But then Dwight McNeil last season: 22 appearances in the Premier League, zero goals, one assist, so he’s not doing enough either."

O'Hara replied: "It’s like ‘We’ll give you crap, you give us crap back. Call it quits, no charge’.

"I like McNeil. If I were to pick which player would I rather have, I’d take Dwight McNeil. He’s going to work hard, with a lovely left foot. He gives you something.

"Brennan Johnson is just so frustrating because he’s got all the attributes."

He added: "Maybe it’s a confidence thing, maybe David Moyes might be the right manager for him. He’s got the right attributes, he showed it at Nottingham Forest."

Statistics, however, can tell a different story. Despite Johnson enduring a rough 18 months for Tottenham and Palace, he has remained far more clinical in the Premier League than McNeil.

Since Johnson was promoted to the top flight with Nottingham Forest, he has scored 37 goals across all competitions. During that same timeframe, McNeil has netted just 15 times.

Looking at goals-per-minute, Everton's new recruit finds the net once every 253 minutes, whereas Palace's newest winger scores just once every 908 minutes.

There is a clear gap in clinical edge. The Merseyside outfit are replacing a player with a similar assist rate while more than doubling their goal threat upfront.

Additionally, Johnson offers output that comes from a versatile, high-tempo, vertical approach instead of the structured, possession-orientated role McNeil occupied.

4 Everton were just three points off the Champions League places with seven games left last season but then imploded Credit: Getty

While O'Hara argued the ex-Forest player was disappointing for Spurs, the 25-year-old finished as the club's top goalscorer in the 2024/25 campaign with a total of 18 goals.

In comparison, Everton have not had a player hit that mark since Romelu Lukaku in 2016/17.

Even when McNeil was the Toffees' top scorer in 2023, he managed a grand total of just seven goals.

What will Johnson add to Everton?

A primary criticism of Everton in recent seasons is that the squad has severely lacked raw speed, particularly under Sean Dyche and David Moyes.

When the Premier League published sprint data in April and highlighted the fastest recorded sprints since the 2020/21 season.

Johnson featured 15th on the list by clocking 36.70 km/h against Manchester City in 2023.

With Spurs' Micky van de Ven and Wolves' Jackson Tchatchoua each appearing twice on that list, statistically only 11 Premier League players have achieved a higher top speed than the 25-year-old.

Moyes can now harness Johnson's explosive pace in counter-attacking setups—a vital asset for an Everton side that registered the fourth-lowest possession average in England's top flight last term.

Sports.title: Scotland told to make U-turn on hiring 51-cap player to get Champions League winning manager
Sports.content:
Scotland told to make U-turn on hiring 51-cap player to get Champions League winning manager

Scotland have been urged to ditch plans to appoint Steven Naismith as their new boss in favour of Rafael Benitez.

Former Scotland international Naismith is the frontrunner to replace Steve Clarke as boss with a decision expected before next month’s Nations League fixtures.



3 Naismith (centre) was part of the Scotland coaching staff for the World Cup qualifiers and the tournament itself Credit: Getty

Naismith was part of Clarke’s backroom team and is being primed for the top job despite having an ill-fated spell as Hearts boss on his managerial roll of honour.

Scotland told to hire Benitez instead

Scottish FA (SFA) chiefs have a huge decision to make on the direction of their next head coach and former midfielder Gary McAllister believes they should cast their net further in the search for a new boss.

Ex-Portugal manager Roberto Martinez and Everton boss David Moyes have also been linked with the vacant role.



However, McAllister, who clocked up 57 caps for his country, believes former Liverpool and Newcastle boss Benitez is the standout name among the current available options.

“With Roberto Martinez and Moyesy, I don’t think they’re gettable,” McAllister told talkSPORT. “The salaries they’ve been working for, I don’t know if the SFA pay that.



“Rafa’s looking for a way back in.”

And it appears that the 61-year-old has been doing some digging of his own on Benitez.

“All the guys I’ve played with in my little, short period at Liverpool and the players that played under Rafa speak so highly of him,” McAllister added.



“The discipline, the preparation. He’s a winner as well, he’s won everything.

“Somebody like that is who you’d want as an international manager. He’s been there, seen it and done it and has got vast amounts of experience.”

3 Rafa Benitez is looking for a way back into football after his sacking as Panathinaikos boss Credit: Getty

The Spaniard has been out of work since being dismissed by Greek giant Panathinakos in May after only managing a fourth-placed finish in the play-offs of the Greek Super League.



McAllister’s recommendation would mean the SFA pulling the plug on Naismith, who already has experience of the national team set-up.

But the ex-Leeds and Liverpool midfielder believes there are no standout names in the running for the job.

“I know it might never happen but there’s no outstanding candidate for me, I don’t see one," McAllister added.

“Steven Naismith, Clarkey’s assistant might just be a step too much for his first job.



"I think Derek McInnes would have been in contention if he hadn’t gone to Glasgow Rangers.”

3 Gary McAllister says he has reservations over the possible appointment of Naismith Credit: talkSPORT

Naismith's record

Naismith’s time in the Hearts dugout saw him pick up a 43.1 per cent win rate.

He was handed the reins on an interim basis following the dismissal of Robbie Neilson before being handed the job full-time in June 2023.



Prior to his spell with the Hearts first team, Naismith worked with the club’s academy to build up his coaching expertise.

He subsequently went on to become the club’s development manager.

Sports.title: Borussia Dortmund scout behind Jude Bellingham and Erling Haaland wanted by Premier League clubs
Sports.content:
Borussia Dortmund scout behind Jude Bellingham and Erling Haaland wanted by Premier League clubs

Newcastle United and Tottenham Hotspur are interested in Borussia Dortmund scout Sebastian Krug, talkSPORT understands.

Krug, who is seen as playing a key role in Dortmund signing Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham, is wanted by a other European clubs.

4 Haaland and Bellingham proved to be two of Dortmund's best ever signings Credit: Getty

The 43-year-old was appointed as Dortmund's chief scout in 2022 and has worked exclusively with the German giants.

Other names that he has scouted and played roles in signing include Jadon Sancho and Jamie Gittens as well.

More recently, he managed to prise Jobe Bellingham away from Sunderland ahead of numerous Premier League sides to continue the Bellingham affiliation with Dortmund.

He identified both of the Bellingham brothers early on and focused on establishing a good connection with the family.

As a result, he is thought to be someone they trust, and this along with several other high-profile purchases has made him of interest.

Newcastle and Spurs are looking to revamp their recruitment models, and the feeling with Krug is he's reached the end of his time of Dortmund after ten years of service.

Krug's buys at Dortmund

In the time that Krug has been at Dortmund, the club have made some seriously impressive transfers.

Since becoming chief scout alone, Karim Adeyemi, Nico Schlotterbeck and Julian Ryerson arrived in his first year.

Felix Nmecha and Serhou Guirassy have also come through the door, while huge sales for Jude, Haaland, Gittens and Donyell Malen have gone through.

4 Gittens was another one who Krug extensively researched Credit: Getty

4 Haaland and Bellingham were sold for a combined fee of over £150million Credit: Getty

Newcastle restructure

Eddie Howe has left St James' Park, and Matthias Jaissle is in.

The Magpies have Howe's cousin Andy in a prominent recruitment role, along with sporting director Ross Wilson.

Wilson has overseen the majority of the business this summer, with Newcastle shifting focus away from domestic recruits to young, European talent.

The oldest player they've signed this summer is new goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek from Braga, and he is only 24,

Long-serving chief scout Steve Nickson is also set to leave once the transfer window closes.

He was responsible for scouting and helping sign some of Newcastle's best players in recent years, including Joelinton, Allan Saint-Maximin, Alexander Isak and Sven Botman.

However, he is set to take on a new role as director of football for Wrexham, meaning Newcastle will need a new chief scout.

4 Isak is one of Nickson's recruits, but Newcastle will need a new man to lead that department Credit: AFP

Jaissle's requirement

New Toon boss Jaissle has promised 'adjustments' to the squad between now and the end of the transfer window.

Speaking at his first press conference at St James' Park, the German made it clear that he is positive about more players arriving on Tyneside before the Toon face Liverpool in their opening match on August 23.

He said: "We are totally aware internally which positions we might need to strengthen the squad.

"But this is nothing for here, for the press conference. We believe in the players that we have now. And we had a chat after the match in Valencia where you were really happy that the young lads getting the chance, so that's also the approach from this club.

"Every minute they're getting, then they can grow.

"Like I said in my first statement, there will be adjustments in the squad. We still have time."

Sports.title: These are the key clues Matthias Jaissle gave away at Newcastle unveiling - from the signings he wants to how he will turn this club around, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
These are the key clues Matthias Jaissle gave away at Newcastle unveiling - from the signings he wants to how he will turn this club around, writes CRAIG HOPE

Unlock more from Craig Hope inside the Newcastle camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

There was no mass of fans on the St James’ Park steps and very little fanfare inside Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle United unveiling.

For a club who want to be among the world's best by 2030, this was an understated arrival for a head coach whose contract takes us through to that date. He is, by that logic, the man the Newcastle hierarchy believe can lead them to the top.

Not that there was any talk of Champions League and Premier League titles here, or questions about signing Kylian Mbappe, as there was at the outset of the Saudi project nearly five years ago. Veteran midfielder Pierre Emile-Hojbjerg, 31, has been the No1 target in recent days.

Rather, this was something of a reality check, and that is no reflection on Jaissle. The German spoke with enthusiasm and intelligence, and he did so alone. There was no sign of chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan or hierarchy on stage with the 38-year-old. No global media, either. This is where Newcastle are at right now, and Jaissle appears smart enough to know what he is walking into – a club where the best players and manager have not long walked out.

His demeanour was one of excitement, composure and, a word he sought to stress more than once, optimism. There is a believable authority about him. But beneath the positivity was a more subtle message. He needs new players. And he needs time.

Sources have suggested Jaissle is already well aware of what the squad he has inherited lacks – leadership and depth of quality in key areas. You took note when he was asked about the departures of senior players and responded by referencing a leadership ‘vacuum’. He is right, too.

There was no mass of fans on the St James’ Park steps and very little fanfare inside Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle United unveiling

Sources have suggested Jaissle is already well aware of what the squad he has inherited lacks – leadership and depth of quality in key areas

So, with Bruno Guimaraes now in north London, does he have a new captain yet? ‘No,’ came the reply. And that was that.

His answer when asked what remit the board had given him for this season was equally revealing, given Eddie Howe and the club made no secret of their expectation of European qualification last term, which ended in 12th place in the Premier League.

‘(The remit) is that we are ambitious, but this will not happen overnight, especially when you have such a big transition phase now,’ he said. ‘It makes no sense to promise you anything, because I don’t know how things look in half a year or one year. What we can control, we will control. Cutting the tasks down on a daily basis, doing the best job, and then we go in the right direction - and that is going to be successful.’

Transition was another word he used repeatedly. In fact, the Newcastle 2.0 that chief executive David Hopkinson has spoken about post-Howe feels, at this moment, more like Newcastle 1.5. Less than two weeks out from the visit of Liverpool in the Premier League opener, Jaissle has no fit full backs, while the experienced midfielder he craves appears no closer to arriving.

‘We are aware of what we need and the squad that we want,’ he said. ‘Internally, everyone is aware of that, and we are working on the solutions.’

There are talks over a deal for Benfica right back Amar Dedic, but he is another who has never played in England. It is not hard to understand why 97-cap Denmark midfielder Hojbjerg, with more than 250 Premier League appearances at Southampton and Tottenham, was seen by Jaissle as the kind of foundation around which a younger team could be rebuilt. The Marseille midfielder, however, has opted against the move. The optics of Newcastle 1.5 are not the easiest sell.

Because when the target of ‘consolidation’ was put to the manager of this Saudi-owned club at his first press conference – and it did not sound ridiculous or provoke a challenge – it told you plenty about the task in front of him. For that, he deserves patience.

‘It's a big challenge,’ he said. ‘It always is when there's a transition period, but it's not the time to complain. It doesn't make sense to see the negative. We want to see the chance in the situation.’

There are talks over a deal for Benfica right back Amar Dedic (left), but he is another who has never played in England

It is not hard to understand why Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg (right) was seen by Jaissle as the kind of foundation around which a younger team could be rebuilt

You suspect Jaissle's demonstrative touchline presence will endear him to Newcastle supporters, if not those of the opposition

There is another challenge for Jaissle – keeping himself out of the stands. Although you suspect a demonstrative touchline presence will endear him to Newcastle supporters, if not those of the opposition.

At times in Valencia during his first game on Saturday night, it looked like he was making overlapping runs beyond right winger Anthony Elanga. Indeed, he has already asked club staff how many bookings a manager is allowed before they serve a touchline ban, and he returned a hesitant laugh when informed it was just three.

‘I will not change my style because that's my personality,’ said the former Al Hilal boss. ‘On the touchline, I am emotional. But I need to respect the technical box a bit more. I had a long line in Saudi Arabia, so I think my GPS would be quite high! I'm a bit scared. I hope in the beginning the referees can maybe close their eyes here and there a little!’

There were other flashes of levity, too, including mention of the song which the Toon Army bestowed on him in Spain – ‘Jaissle, I can boogie’ to the tune of Baccara’s Yes Sir, I Can Boogie. ‘I heard it once and I was smiling,’ he said. ‘The guys around me, all the staff members, said they're really looking forward to sitting after a match in the bar and listening to the song. So let's see about that.’

To sit in the bar and be serenaded will need wins. To get those wins, at least on a consistent enough basis to make a success of his debut season, will need more players of greater experience and quality. He knows that. Maybe it is, then, that a low-key introduction was what was necessary. There is no need for Jaissle to boogie just yet. First, he needs a team to dance with.

Sports.title: UEFA don't want clubs like Aston Villa to win. They've forced them to sell their best players, as 'bigger' clubs lose hundreds of millions with impunity. But thanks to Unai Emery, Villa are beating the system, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
UEFA don't want clubs like Aston Villa to win. They've forced them to sell their best players, as 'bigger' clubs lose hundreds of millions with impunity. But thanks to Unai Emery, Villa are beating the system, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Aston Villa camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Forget what European football chiefs might say in public. Aston Villa are unwelcome guests at tonight’s party in Salzburg and the game’s wealthy elite would be perfectly happy if they never turned up again.

If that sounds harsh, read the thoughts of UEFA finance chief Andrea Traverso. Speaking last year about financial rules that seem to reward money-making activities over anything that happens on the pitch, Traverso admitted ‘the regulations were never designed to create competitive balance but rather to bring financial discipline, and that stability is precisely what continues to attract investors to European football’.

In the interview with the Football Benchmark group, Traverso also accepts that ‘if the financial gap between clubs continues to grow, it becomes harder to maintain that competitive balance’. But if that is a priority for UEFA, they have a funny way of showing it.

If they beat Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup tonight, Villa will collect a second European trophy in less than three months, following their Europa League triumph in May. They are about to start their second Champions League campaign in three seasons and under Unai Emery, they have finished seventh, fourth, sixth and fourth in the Premier League. Their progress has been astonishing.

Instead of being able to build on that, Villa have had to sell their best attacker and best midfielder this summer, as well as France’s left back, just to satisfy UEFA’s financial controls.

Their best defender, Ezri Konsa, is wanted by Arsenal and Emery hopes he will not follow Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne through the exit door.

Aston Villa's progress under Unai Emery has been astonishing - and now they have a chance of a second European trophy in three months

But they have been hamstrung by the financial rules of UEFA and the Premier League, leaving them with little choice but to sell star men like Morgan Rogers (pictured)

Even though Villa co-owners Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens are worth a combined £10billion, Villa are effectively being punished because they cannot generate the same revenue as commercial giants like Manchester United, Tottenham and Chelsea.

If Villa qualify for Europe’s top competition again this season, they could start to dream of challenging their richer rivals long-term. If they do, it might just be the greatest achievement of Emery’s top-level career.

Why did Villa have to sell?
